Title: Bank account opening using Singpass and MyInfo
KeyTerms: Finance, Financial Inclusion, e-KYC, Know-Your-Customer, MyInfo, Customer onboarding, Digital Onboarding, Paperless Banking
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor authentication (OTP and Singpass Face Verification (SFV))
Description:
Banks in Singapore use Singpass as a trusted authentication method for digital onboarding and account opening. A customer starts account opening through the bank’s app or website, authenticates with Singpass, and then consents to share verified identity attributes through MyInfo.
The MyInfo service enables customers to auto-populate all the necessary details. As a result, there is no need to manually enter personal details or upload identity documents scans, since key attributes, such as name, address, date of birth, and government-verified identifiers are retrieved directly from authoritative sources. 

When higher assurance is required, Singpass Face Verification is used as an additional authentication modality. This helps reduce the risks of impersonation or synthetic identity fraud. 

For banks, the workflow improves data accuracy and enables faster decision-making, while customers benefit from fewer forms and shorter wait times.

Title: Access to an education and career platform by students using a national digital ID
KeyTerms: Education, academic and career guidance, knowledge sharing
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - Single-factor based authentication
Description:
Students in the Democratic Republic of the Congo make education and career choices without reliable guidance or verified information. Training institutions also struggle to track student progress because student records remain fragmented. This problem weakens links between education, skills, and jobs.
The use case proposes a digital platform linked to the national digital ID system. The platform creates a verified learner identity for each student. Students can access information on schools, vocational training, scholarships, careers, and skills pathways through mobile or web channels. This platform also stores verified academic records, certifications, and career interests in one secure profile.
Accredited teachers and institutions publish verified courses through institutional digital identities. Students can access premium content through mobile money linked to their digital ID. The platform supports local languages, offers offline access, and secure authentication for low-connectivity areas in the country.

Title: Access to the agriculture services platform using the national digital ID
KeyTerms: Agriculture, artificial intelligence, digital identity
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - Single factor authentication
Description:
Farmers across West Africa face climate shocks, low productivity, and weak access to markets and financial services. Smallholder farmers also lack trusted digital identities and reliable agricultural information. These issues limit access to subsidies, insurance, credit, and modern farming support.
The use case proposes a digital agriculture platform linked to a secure national digital ID system. Each farmer creates a verified farmer profile, which provides them with access to the platform. The platform provides crop advice for farmers, weather alerts, subsidies, insurance, and microcredit services. Farmers can authenticate through biometrics or mobile-based verification, even in low-connectivity areas.
The platform uses artificial intelligence (AI) to provide localized advice based on crop type, farm location, and farming history. Farmers receive voice-based guidance in local languages on irrigation, planting, fertilizer use, and pest control. This platform also creates a verified farming profile that helps governments, cooperatives, and financial institutions deliver targeted services and reduce fraud.

Title: Access to an integrated public service delivery platform using a national digital ID
KeyTerms: Unique identification, digital identity
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - Single-factor authentication
Description:
Residents in Senegal still use multiple identification numbers and paper documents to access public services. This issue creates duplicate records, delays, identity fraud, and inconsistent data across government agencies. Public institutions also face challenges in real-time identity verification.
The use case proposes a unified digital identity platform built around a national digital identity. The platform links national ID cards, passports, driver’s licenses, tax records, health records, and student IDs through an interoperable digital ID system and a centralized population registry.
Citizens can authenticate through biometrics, one-time passwords (OTPs), or digital credentials linked to their national ID. Government agencies access only the data needed for their services through consent-based controls. This platform also supports real-time verification, reduces duplicate registrations, and improves service delivery. Automated alerts inform citizens about approvals, renewals, and document collection. Audit trails and consent logs also strengthen accountability and data protection.

Title: Issuance of an administrative document using a national digital ID in Senegal
KeyTerms: Public administration, technological innovation, public services
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - OTP-based authentication
Description:
Citizens in Senegal lack easy access to official documents and public services. This problem affects rural communities the most. 
The proposed platform links the issuance of administrative documents with the national digital ID system. Citizens access the platform through mobile or web channels. They authenticate their identity through OTP-based verification. The platform retrieves verified data from government registries to reduce manual data entry. Optical character recognition (OCR) tools digitize and verify supporting documents. The system routes applications to the department concerned for approval.
Citizens track application status in real time, receive alerts, and download approved digital records securely. A multilingual chatbot guides the user through each step.

Title: National digital identity-enabled agriculture service platform for small farmers
KeyTerms: Agriculture, digital identity, technological innovation, platform-based solutions, small farmers
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - Single-factor authentication through OTP or biometrics
Description:
Smallholder farmers across Africa often lack access to subsidies, credit, insurance, and formal markets because they lack trusted identity records or verified farm data. This weakens financial inclusion and limits access to government support. Farmers also struggle to access timely weather updates, crop advisory services, and disease alerts.
The proposed platform creates a verified digital farmer profile and connects it with their national digital ID. Farmers use digital ID-based authentication through OTP verification on mobile devices or through biometrics at local centers. The profile links identity data to farm records, such as land size, crop history, and location details.
Government agencies, financial institutions, and cooperatives use the platform to verify eligibility for subsidies, loans, insurance, and market programs. AI-based tools provide crop advice, weather alerts, and support for disease detection. The platform supports local languages, offline access, and simple mobile interfaces to improve service delivery in rural communities.

Title: Access to public services by using the national digital ID
KeyTerms: Digital identity, public administration, public services
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - Single-factor authentication to access public services
Description:
Citizens across Senegal and West Africa face slow and fragmented public services. Paper-based systems increase delays, fraud, duplicate records, and exclusion, especially in rural areas. Citizens also struggle to access healthcare, banking, education, and social protection services because providers cannot verify identity easily.
The proposed platform creates a secure and interoperable digital identity ecosystem linked to biometric credentials and government registries. Citizens enroll with fingerprint or facial authentication, and the system creates a trusted digital identity for them. They then access services through digital ID-based authentication based on biometrics, one-time passwords (OTPs), or unstructured supplementary service data (USSD) channels.
Government agencies and authorized providers verify identities through interoperable application programming interfaces (APIs). This platform supports electronic medical records, digital financial services, scholarship delivery, pension access, and voter registration. Consent-based verification and role-based access controls protect personal data.

Title: National digital identity-enabled health record platform
KeyTerms: Health, innovation, geolocation-based solutions
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - Single-factor authentication using biometrics to provide consent-based data sharing
Description:
African countries still use paper-based medical records. Patients often visit different hospitals without a shared medical history. This issue leads to repeated tests, delayed treatment, duplicate prescriptions, and weak follow-up care, especially in rural areas.
The proposed platform links health records to the national digital ID system and creates a digital health profile for each citizen. Healthcare providers verify patient identity through biometrics or OTP-based authentication and access medical records instantly. The platform stores consultations, prescriptions, vaccination history, laboratory reports, and treatment details in one trusted system.
Citizens access records through a mobile application and share data securely through quick response (QR) codes or consent-based access. Healthcare workers can update records online or offline, with automatic synchronization when an internet connection is available. Encrypted data exchange and audit trails protect patient information.

Title: Digital blood donation and supply platform using national digital ID
KeyTerms: Health, digital optimization of blood donation services, Innovation, healthcare, digital technologies
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - Single-factor authentication
Description:
African countries face blood shortages due to weak donor records, low voluntary donations, and poor coordination between blood banks and hospitals. Rural communities often struggle to access safe blood during emergencies, maternal care, and chronic disease treatment. Health facilities also find it difficult to quickly identify eligible donors in urgent situations.
This use case proposes a digital blood donation and supply platform linked to the national digital ID system. Citizens register through a mobile app, web portal, or USSD channel with biometric or one-time password (OTP)-based authentication. This platform creates a verified donor profile that stores information such as blood type and donation history. Health workers authenticate donors through the national digital ID system and update records in real time. Blood banks and hospitals track blood stock across facilities and coordinate redistribution during shortages. The platform also sends targeted alerts to eligible donors based on blood type, location, and urgency.

Title: Digital platform for seed traceability and certification using national digital ID
KeyTerms: Agriculture, agricultural development, food security, agricultural data traceability
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - Single-factor authentication across the seed supply chain
Description:
African countries face major crop losses due to counterfeit and low-quality seeds. Weak certification systems and poor producer records prevent farmers from verifying seed quality and origin. Farmers often buy uncertified seeds, which reduce crop yield, increase disease risk, and lower farm income. 

The use case proposes a digital seed traceability and certification platform that connects to the national digital ID system. The proposed platform creates a digital seed passport for every certified seed batch and links it to the verified digital identity of producers, distributors, cooperatives, and retailers. Regulators register each certified batch with a unique digital identifier that stores seed variety, origin, treatment history, and certification details. Every transaction across the supply chain uses digital authentication and creates a traceable record. 

Farmers verify seed authenticity through a quick response (QR) code or near-field communication (NFC) tag before purchase. The platform helps regulators detect counterfeit seeds, improve accountability, and strengthen food security.

Title: Access to agricultural subsidies by women farmers using the national digital ID
KeyTerms: Women, agriculture, climate change, grants, financial education
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - Single Factor authentication using OTP
Description:
Women farmers in Morocco face barriers in subsidy access. Weak land records and low literacy limit participation. Systems often fail to recognize women’s ownership or rights to use the land. As a result, many eligible women do not receive benefits, and delivery lacks transparency.  

The proposed platform links the national digital ID to land records for each parcel, which links the land to owners and female family members. It creates verified records of land-use rights. Women authenticate their identity through biometrics, either directly or with agent support. 

After verification, women check schemes and initiate subsidy claims via USSD/SMS or service points. The system issues subsidies as digital entitlements. Women redeem them through approved cooperatives and a one-time password (OTP) linked to their national digital ID. This approach improves targeting, reduces leakage, and ensures secure access.

Title: Access to the local job opportunities for skilled workers and artisans using the national digital ID
KeyTerms: Public infrastructure development, mobile application solutions, service delivery, geotagging
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - Single-factor authentication to link profile with national digital ID
Description:
Skilled people in construction, public works, and the artisan sectors struggle to find steady work. Masons, carpenters, and mechanics travel daily to search for jobs, which wastes time and reduces income. The proposed use case is a digital platform that links workers with employers.
A worker creates a verified profile through their national digital ID. The profile shows skills, rates, and location. Similarly, employers and individuals post job requests through their national digital ID-linked profile. They can also view nearby workers and contact those with the required skills directly.
This platform improves job access and reduces daily uncertainty. It also builds trust through verified identities. Local skills become visible, and workers gain a more consistent income.

Title: Digital proof of life using CPF/gov.br
KeyTerms: Digital Proof of Life, Good Governance, Public Service Delivery
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: Residents in Brazil can generate their proof of life digitally. The system uses the CPF as a unique identifier to process the request. Residents authenticate themselves through a gov.br login to confirm their identity. The system integrates biometric data from the Electoral Justice (TSE) database with records from the National Institute of Social Security (INSS) to perform face authentication during the process.

Title: Vehicle Registration using ThaID/NDID
KeyTerms: Government e-services, Public Service Delivery
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor Authentication
Description: Thailand uses ThaID and National Digital ID (NDID) for vehicle registration. Individuals can authenticate their identity through facial verification using the ThaID app or NDID federated login. The system confirms the user’s identity and routes the authentication result to the Department of Land Transport (DLT) portal. The portal then automatically retrieves the individual’s verified personal data. This enables individuals to avail services, such as annual vehicle re-registration, vehicle tax payment, initiation of an ownership transfer, and retrieval of registration certificate status, entirely online.

Title: Single Sign On (SSO) using ThaID and NDID
KeyTerms: Single sign-on, Government e-services, Public Service Delivery
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor Authentication
Description: Thailand’s digital government ecosystem integrates ThaID and National Digital ID (NDID) across multiple government portals for single sign-on access. Citizens can authenticate using facial verification through the ThaID mobile application or NDID federated login through licensed identity providers. After successful authentication, the system securely routes the confirmation to the relying government portal. This enables the user to access services, such as digital approvals, complaint submission, court services, and regulatory filings.

Title: Bank account opening using NDID/ThaID
KeyTerms: NDID, ThaID, eKYC, Banking, Insurance, Customer onboarding, Digital Onboarding, Paperless Banking
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor Authentication
Description: Thailand’s National Digital ID (NDID) platform enables in-person or remote e-KYC processes across banking, insurance, and lending sectors. Customers initiate onboarding through a bank or financial institution’s application and choose an identity provider, such as ThaID or a licensed bank app. Authentication is completed using multi-factor methods, including one-time password (OTP) or personal identification number (PIN) and face authentication. Identity is verified against the Department of Provincial Administration (DOPA) registry. On successful verification, verified details are shared with banks and insurance companies.

Title: Tax filing using NDID/ThaID
KeyTerms: Income Tax, Tax filing
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor Authentication
Description: The Revenue Department in Thailand supports secure online tax filing. Taxpayers authenticate themselves using National Digital ID (NDID) or ThaID credentials. Taxpayers log in to the e-filing portal using their 13-digit personal identification number and OTP- or NDID-based authentication. For NDID-based verification, the user approves the authentication request through their chosen identity provider, such as ThaID or a participating bank app. Upon successful identity verification, individuals file tax returns.

Title: Sim Registration (eKYC) via NDID/ThaID
KeyTerms: KYC, Electronic Know Your Customer (eKYC), SIM registration, Customer Onboarding, Digital Onboarding
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor Authentication
Description: The National Broadcasting and Telecommunications Commission (NBTC) mandates that customers link a valid identification (ID) with a SIM when they purchase and register SIM cards in Thailand. During onboarding, service providers verify the customer’s identity information against the central registry, which is maintained by the Department of Provincial Administration (DOPA). This verification is conducted through National Digital ID (NDID) or ThaID using biometric authentication. Upon successful verification, the provider completes the SIM registration process.

Title: Access e-government Services using Singpass
KeyTerms: Single sign-on, Government e-services, Public Service Delivery
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: Singpass serves as the primary mechanism for to access government e-services. Singpass holders can select “Log in with Singpass” on a government website or mobile application and complete authentication through the Singpass app, with a 6‑digit passcode, device biometrics, or an OTP. Login with Singpass also acts as a single sign-on, which allows users to access various services across government agencies. In-person service counters also accept Singpass-based verification for faster service delivery.

Title: Access to income support by low-wage workers by using Singpass
KeyTerms: Social Protection, Social Security, Government Disbursement
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor authentication (OTP and Singpass Face Verification (SFV))
Description: Launched in 2007, the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) program provides cash payments and Central Provident Fund (CPF) top-ups to boost the income and retirement savings of lower-wage workers. Beneficiaries can authenticate with Singpass to access WIS e-services, such as to check eligibility, view payment amounts, and update bank account details for disbursement. Singpass is also used to log in for special payouts, such as the Workfare Special Payment (WSP).

Title: Access to cash benefits by low-income seniors  using Singpass
KeyTerms: Social Protection, Social Security, Government Disbursement
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor authentication (OTP and Singpass Face Verification (SFV))
Description: Singpass serves as the authentication method to check the eligibility for, or update the details under, the Silver Support Scheme. Administered by the Ministry of Manpower, the scheme provides quarterly cash support to low-income seniors. Eligibility assessment and payment disbursement are automated through the Central Provident Fund (CPF) digital services. As of 2025, nearly 290,000 Singapore Citizens aged 65 years and above currently benefit from this scheme.

Title: Access to healthcare services using Singpass
KeyTerms: HealthHub, Health records, Appointments, Vaccination records
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor authentication (OTP and Singpass Face Verification (SFV))
Description: Singpass is the standard authentication method to access HealthHub, Singapore’s national digital healthcare platform for personal health services. Users authenticate through Singpass to view and manage sensitive health information, such as health records, vaccinations, test results, and medication-related details, and to book or manage appointments. Singpass users can book an appointment remotely or at clinics or hospitals. Since HealthHub stores sensitive personal health data, two-factor authentication has been mandatory for accessing it since 2017.

Title: e-Stamping using Singpass
KeyTerms: e-Stamping, Property Transactions, Housing Serivces
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor authentication (OTP and Singpass Face Verification (SFV))
Description: Housing and property-related e-services can be accessed using Singpass. The users can submit documents for stamping, retrieve stamp certificates, and manage stamping records through Singpass authentication.

Title: e-Sign using Singpass
KeyTerms: e-Sign, Digital Signature, Secure Electronic Signature
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor authentication (OTP and Singpass Face Verification (SFV))
Description: The ‘Sign with Singpass’ service allows individuals to digitally sign documents. Built on the Singpass ecosystem, it enables users to sign contracts and other agreements remotely through the Singpass app. Signatures created through ‘Sign with Singpass’ are legally recognized as secure electronic signatures under Singapore’s Electronic Transactions Act 2010. They are legally binding and accepted by both government agencies and private organizations. Parties can sign documents instantly and securely without the need to be in the same place or sign physical papers.

Title: e-KYC for SIM/e-SIM issuance using Singpass
KeyTerms: KYC, Electronic Know Your Customers (eKYC), SIM registration, Customer Onboarding, Digital Onboarding
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor authentication (OTP and Singpass Face Verification (SFV))
Description: Singpass holders can self-register for a SIM card in Singapore. The users can initiate a SIM registration activation request through the telecom service provider's app or website and verify their identity through Singpass. This process ties the activation to the correct person and reduces risks, such as identity impersonation and fraudulent activations. It also improves customer experience by allowing fast self-service activation while maintaining compliance with identity requirements for mobile services.

Title: Tax Filing using Singpass
KeyTerms: Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS), Income Tax, Tax filing
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor authentication (OTP and Singpass Face Verification (SFV))
Description:
The Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) operates the Singapore tax portal that offers various services to taxpayers. Taxpayers authenticate themselves through Singpass to access the portal. After successful authentication, taxpayers can submit returns, review tax assessments, manage payments, and receive official communication. 

The MyInfo service enables taxpayers to pre-fill their details from verified government sources, which reduces errors and simplifies the process. As these services involve sensitive personal and financial information, strong authentication mechanisms are needed to prevent unauthorised access. Hence, two-factor authentication (2FA), including Singpass Face Verification, is mandatory to file taxes and access other selective services on the tax portal.

Title: Access to financial data using Singpass and SGFinDex
KeyTerms: SGFinDex, Financial Data Exchange, Open Banking, Financial Planning, Data Consolidation, Consolidated View, Wealth Management
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor authentication (OTP and Singpass Face Verification (SFV))
Description:
Singapore Financial Data Exchange (SGFinDex) is a national platform that enables individuals to retrieve and view their financial information from multiple sources, such as banks, insurers, and selected government agencies. 

Singpass serves as the primary authentication and consent mechanism, which enables users to authorize the retrieval of data from various institutions in any third-party application. Users can consolidate their financial information into a single view instead of logging into each provider separately. 

The financial data may include account balances, loans, insurance policies, and relevant government-held information, such as central provCPF or tax records. 
The financial data may include account balances, loans, insurance policies, and relevant government-held information, such as the Central Provident Fund (CPF) or tax records.
 
SGFinDex itself does not store data; it merely acts as the transmission rail between institutions. As of late 2024, SGFinDex has supported more than 150,000 users and facilitated more than 620,000 data retrievals.

Title: Access to public service through Modern Ethiopia Service for Organised Benefits (MESOB) platform
KeyTerms: Public Services, Digital Government, One-Stop-Shop, Service Delivery, Government Efficiency, Citizen Access, MESOB
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - OTP-based authentication
Description:
In April 2025, the Modern Ethiopia Service for Organized Benefits (MESOB) was launched as an integrated one-stop shop for multiple government services. The pilot involved 12 federal government ministries that offered 41 public services in a paperless, fully digital format at the MESOB centers. During the pilot’s initial months, more than 12,000 users availed services at MESOB with a 90% satisfaction rate. In June 2025, Deputy Prime Minister Temesgen Tiruneh announced the nationwide rollout of MESOB. 

MESOB functions as a single-stop public service delivery platform that enables citizens with Fayda digital IDs to access a wide range of services and reduces the need for them to physically visit institutions multiple times. Citizens can access services through the web portal, mobile application, or physical MESOB service centers for human assistance. 

Currently, the program uses OTP-based authentication and QR code-based offline verification when the Fayda authentical service is inaccessible. Biometric authentication through face and fingerprint is planned for future implementation.

Title: Digital farmer registry for agricultural support
KeyTerms: Agriculture, Digital Identity, Financial Inclusion, Farmer Registry, Extension Services, Microfinance Access, Agricultural Transformation
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - OTP-based online authentication
Description:
The Farmer Profile Project by the Ministry of Agriculture in Ethiopia runs in collaboration with the Agricultural Transformation Institute (ATI). It uses the Fayda ID to create a comprehensive registry of farmer profiles. 

The project addresses the critical barrier of inaccessible, non-interoperable farmer data, which hampers digital service delivery. It involves data collection, validation, integration, and enhancement of existing farmer-centric databases.

Title: Digital ID for refugees
KeyTerms: Refugee
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description:
The National ID Program (NIDP), the UNHCR, and the Refugee and Returnee Service (RRS) signed a data-sharing agreement in January 2024. Since then, efforts have been made to enroll more than 1 million refugees in the Fayda ID system in Ethiopia. The goal is to provide refugees with access to healthcare, education, and telecommunications, among others. 
Under this agreement, the PRIMES Interoperability Gateway (PING) is used to exchange data between national authorities and UNHCR to issue identity cards to refugees and asylum-seekers. 

By the end of 2026, Ethiopia plans to issue about 90,000 Fayda digital ID numbers to refugees and returnees.

Title: Digital ID for students
KeyTerms: Education
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: Ethiopia’s National ID Program and Ministry of Education have adopted the Fayda digital ID as the official student ID across educational institutions. Student biometric data is captured and migrated into the National ID Program's system for Fayda ID generation. The Fayda ID serves as the primary identity credential across academic platforms and streamlines admissions, record management, and national exams.

Title: Tax ID (TIN) registration
KeyTerms: Tax, Finance, Income Tax
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: Digital ID can be used to improve tax administration. In December 2023, Ethiopia began the integration of taxpayer registration with Fayda ID (National digital ID of Ethiopia) to curb tax evasion and fraud in tax-filing and reduce revenue loss. Since then, each new taxpayer identification number (TIN) is mandatorily linked to the Fayda ID number. In the first six months, the Ministry of Revenue issued 128,000 new TINs through the Fayda ID.

Title: Mandatory Digital ID integration with bank accounts for financial inclusion
KeyTerms: Finance, Digital Identity, Financial Inclusion, e-KYC, Know-Your-Customer, Biometric Authentication, National Banking Policy
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description:
The National Bank of Ethiopia and the National ID Program (NIDP) jointly announced a mandatory digital ID integration initiative for banking in November 2023. The rollout followed a phased plan. The pilot began in Addis Ababa on 1st January 2025, followed by expansion to major cities in Ethiopia on 1st July 2025, and a nationwide rollout on 1st January 2026. As per the plan, all bank account holders must link accounts to Fayda IDs by 31st December 2026. 

The initiative uses Fayda, Ethiopia’s national digital ID, for electronic know your customer (e-KYC) processes and enables reliable real-time identity verification during customer onboarding, the launch of digital products, and financial risk control. 

A time-and-motion study revealed significant efficiency gains. Banks reported time savings of 17% to 63%. Notably, an institution even reduced account opening from 43 minutes to 9 minutes through Fayda-based e-KYC.

Title: Social safety net (cash transfer) program
KeyTerms: Social security, Social Protection, Conditional cash transfers
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: Digital ID enables beneficiary verification in Tanzania's flagship social safety net program. The Productive Social Safety Net (PSSN), operational since 2012 and managed by the Tanzania Social Action Fund (TASAF) under the Ministry of Finance, uses NIN to verify beneficiaries who receive cash transfers and other social assistance. TASAF verifies beneficiary identities through the national identification number (NIN) against the National Identification Authority (NIDA) database to ensure transfers reach legitimate recipients and prevent fraud or duplicate enrollments. As of early 2025, PSSN has benefited around 1.37 million households, which cover about 5.2 million individuals. Each household receives between 35,000 and 43,000 TZS (~USD 15-19) per payment cycle. The program's second phase has a total allocation of approximately USD 883.3 million, funded by the World Bank/IDA, government contributions, and multiple development partners.

Title: Social security schemes registration
KeyTerms: Social Security, Social Protection, Pension
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description:
Digital ID verifies and authenticates individuals who register for social security programs and seek to access benefits. Tanzania operates multiple contributory social security programs under the Social Security Regulatory Authority (SSRA), which uses the national identification number (NIN) to verify members against the National Identification Authority (NIDA) database.
 
The National Social Security Fund (NSSF) provides social security coverage to private-sector workers, NGOs, religious organizations, international organizations, and self-employed persons, with employers and employees each contributing 10% of their monthly salaries. 
As of June 2023, NSSF had approximately 1,189,222 registered members. 

The Public Service Social Security Fund (PSSSF), operational since 2018, serves public service employees across mainland Tanzania with contributions from both employers and employees. 

The National Informal Sector Social Security Program (NISS), launched in 2021, extends social insurance coverage to informal-sector workers with flexible payment methods that require a minimum monthly contribution of 30,000 TZS (approximately USD 11.4). 
NISS beneficiaries use their NIN to log in to online platforms and mobile apps to view contributions, update personal information, submit claims, and access services. 

NIN verification ensures accurate member identification, prevents duplicate registrations, streamlines contributions tracking, facilitates benefits disbursement, and enables members to access their social security accounts across different programs throughout their working lives.

Title: Driver's license issuance and motor vehicle registration
KeyTerms: Transport, Vehicle registration, Identity verification
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: Digital ID verifies individuals who apply for driver's licenses and register motor vehicles. The Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA) operates the Integrated Domestic Revenue Administration System (IDRAS), which includes computerized driver's license and motor vehicle registration systems. During driver's license application through the TRA Taxpayer Portal, applicants must provide their national identification number (NIN) for identity verification against the National Identification Authority (NIDA) database. For motor vehicle registration, the central motor vehicle registration system requires vehicle owners to provide their NIN as part of the ownership details when they complete registration, re-registration, change of ownership, or other vehicle-related transactions.

Title: ChanjoCovid (COVID-19 vaccination) application
KeyTerms: Health services, Vaccination management, Digital health
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description:
Digital ID verified citizens' identities when they accessed Coronavirus (COVID-19) vaccination services through the ChanjoCovid portal developed by the Tanzania Ministry of Health. The national identification number (NIN) is one of the accepted identification documents to book vaccination appointments and access vaccination certificates on the platform. 

The ChanjoCovid system, a COVID-19-specific instance hosted on Tanzania's District Health Information System (DHIS2), support data collection, reporting, and monitoring of vaccination services nationwide. Citizens could use their NIN to register for vaccination, book appointments at vaccination centers, and retrieve their electronic vaccination certificates that comply with international requirements. 

By April 2023, around 38.9 million vaccine doses had been distributed and administered through the ChanjoCovid application, which achieve 51% vaccination coverage of the total population, a dramatic increase from 2.8% in January 2022.

Title: Registration for National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF)
KeyTerms: Health insurance, Social protection
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description:
Digital ID verifies citizens' identities during National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF) registration and service access in Tanzania. National identification number (NIN) is required for NHIF registration, whether completed online through the NHIF self-service portal or in person at an NHIF office. 

During registration, members must provide their NIN and personal details, such as name, email address, and cell phone number. The system verifies the NIN against the National Identification Authority (NIDA) database to accurately validate identity and prevent fraudulent enrollments. 

As of June 2023, NHIF had around 1,368,314 contributing members with about 5 million beneficiaries. NIN integration helps NHIF maintain accurate member records, prevent duplicate registrations, streamline claims processing, and ensure health insurance coverage reaches legitimate beneficiaries across all membership categories.

Title: Passport application
KeyTerms: Travel document, Identity verification
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description:
Digital ID facilitates identity verification during passport issuance. The Tanzania Immigration Department verifies applicants' identities by matching their national identification numbers (NINs) against the National Identification Authority (NIDA) database during passport applications. Since January 2018, Tanzania has issued biometric East African e-passports that comply with International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) international standards. 
During a passport application, whether online through the immigration portal or in person at a regional immigration office, applicants must provide their NIN for identity verification. The process includes complete biometric capture, with fingerprints and facial images recorded in the immigration database during in-person appointments at regional offices, Immigration Headquarters, or Tanzanian embassies abroad.

Title: Registration for Tax Identification Number (TIN)
KeyTerms: Tax registration, e-KYC, Tax compliance
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - NIN-based online authentication
Description:
Digital ID enables real-time identity validation during tax identification number (TIN) registration through the Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA) Taxpayer Portal. When taxpayers apply for a TIN online, the system authenticates their national identification number (NIN) against the National Identification Authority (NIDA) database to verify identity. 

The portal offers two registration pathways: with NIN (for Tanzanian citizens and residents) or without NIN (for foreign nationals who use a passport, driver’s license, voter's ID, or Zanzibar ID). For those with NIN, the system first checks registration status to prevent duplicate TINs, as each individual can have only one TIN. 
The portal provides 24/7 self-service TIN registration, which eliminates the need for physical office visits in most cases.

Title: Business registrations and licensing
KeyTerms: Business registration, Company incorporation, e-KYC
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - NIN-based online authentication
Description:
Digital ID verifies identity during business registrations and company incorporations through the Online Registration System (ORS) of the Business Registrations and Licensing Agency (BRELA). The national identification number (NIN) is mandatory for all users to create an ORS account and access business registration services in Tanzania. Shareholders, directors, and business owners must provide their NIN during the registration process for their companies, business names, trademarks, and patents. 

For Tanzanian nationals and residents, NIN serves as the primary identity verification mechanism. Directors also require a tax identification number (TIN). The ORS system, launched in January 2018, has digitized all business registration and post-registration services, such as annual returns filing, change notifications for companies, and business license applications.

Title: Scholarships and education loan application
KeyTerms: Education, Student verification, e-KYC
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: Digital ID verifies students' identities during loan and scholarship applications. As of May 2025, the Higher Education Students' Loans Board (HESLB) has made the national identification number (NIN) mandatory for all students who apply for education loans. Students must provide their NIN during the application process. The  National Identification Authority (NIDA) database then verifies the NIN to ensure accurate identity verification and prevent fraud. In the 2024-2025 academic year, around 245,799 students were expected to receive HESLB loans. NIN verification helps ensure loans reach legitimate beneficiaries and improves accountability in education financing.

Title: Bank account opening
KeyTerms: Financial services, e-KYC, AML/CFT
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Fingerprint authentication
Description: Digital ID enables electronic know your customer (e-KYC) to validate identity to open bank accounts. Under Bank of Tanzania (BOT) KYC and Anti-Money Laundering/Combating the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) regulations, banks and microfinance institutions must verify customer identity during account opening. The national identification number (NIN) serves as the primary proof of identity. Financial institutions verify customers through fingerprint authentication against the National Identification Authority (NIDA) database. As of 2023, more than 55 financial institutions had integrated with the National ID System, which enabled more than 16 million people to access financial services through their NIN.

Title: SIM card registration
KeyTerms: Telecom, e-KYC
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Fingerprint authentication
Description: Digital ID enables electronic know your customer (e-KYC) verification to validate identity before issuing a SIM card. In Tanzania, national identification number (NIN) can be used to verify a customer's identity. Telecom companies can verify fingerprints against the National Identification Authority (NIDA) database at their service centers. As of 2023, NIDA has registered 53 million out of 54 million SIM card subscribers through NIN.

Title: Bank account opening using PhilSys
KeyTerms: Financial Inclusion, e-KYC, Know-Your-Customer, Digital onboarding
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Biometric authentication (face verification) for e-KYC
Description: Banks in the Philippines use Philippine Identification System (PhilSys) as official proof of identity for customer onboarding and account opening. Customers enter their details, such as name and date of birth, and complete a facial liveness verification through the bank’s mobile app or website. The bank then connects to the National ID eVerify platform to verify the customer’s identity against the PhilSys Registry. After successful identity verification, the platform shares the verified details with the bank. This process eliminates manual document checks, which in turn reduces processing time and cost.

Title: e-Wallet onboarding using PhilSys
KeyTerms: Financial Inclusion, e-KYC, Know-Your-Customer, Digital onboarding
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Biometric authentication (face verification) for e-KYC
Description: Leading e-wallets, such as GCash and HelloMoney, utilize the Philippine Identification System (PhilSys) authentication for account creation and verification. Customers enter their details, such as name and date of birth, and complete a facial liveness check through the e-wallet mobile app. An e-wallet account is created upon successful identity verification. This enables fast, remote financial access for millions, such as those in remote areas.

Title: Access to healthcare services via PhilSys
KeyTerms: Health records, Vaccination records, Health Centre
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Biometric authentication (face verification) for e-KYC
Description: In the Philippines, residents use their Philippine Identification System (PhilSys) credentials to access their PhilHealth membership details and track their claims history online. They can also enroll with various accredited health providers across the country using their national ID. During a PhilHealth transaction, the PhilSys verification platform authenticates credentials in real time to confirm the ID's validity. This immediate check validates the identity and prevents fraud.

Title: Civil Registry applications using PhilSys
KeyTerms: Government e-services, Public Service Delivery
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Biometric authentication (face verification) for e-KYC
Description: The Philippine Identification System (PhilSys) number enables the application of civil registry documents, such as certificates of live birth, no marriage, and death. The PhilSys registry verifies the identity of each holder against its records using biometric authentication through fingerprint scans or face verification for real-time matching. On successful authentication, the application is approved.

Title: Access to the food safety program using PhilSys
KeyTerms: Social Protection, Social Security, Government Disbursement
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Biometric authentication (face verification) for e-KYC
Description: The Philippine Identification System (PhilSys) number and the electronic Philippine Identification (e-PhilID) verify the identity of beneficiaries in the country. The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), under the zero-hunger food voucher program, distributes pre-loaded cards to enrolled households for food purchases. This approach supports targeted assistance delivery and ensures that benefits reach verified recipients.

Title: Access to the conditional cash transfer using PhilSys
KeyTerms: Social Benefit, Social Security, Conditional Cash Transfer
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Biometric authentication (face verification) for e-KYC
Description: In the Philippines, the Philippine Identification System (PhilSys) number and the electronic Philippine Identification (e-PhilID) card are used to verify the identity of beneficiaries. The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), under the national poverty reduction strategy and the conditional cash transfer (CCT) program, provides CCTs to poor households. Beneficiaries are authenticated using fingerprints and facial recognition during family development sessions (FDS).

Title: SIM card registration
KeyTerms: Telecom, eKYC
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - OTP required
Description: Digital ID verifies customer identities during SIM card registration and activation through the National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) verification service. The NIN-SIM linkage has been mandatory for all mobile subscribers in Nigeria since 2020, which includes legal resident foreign nationals. Subscribers submit their national identification number (NIN) to their mobile network operator, which then validates it against the NIMC National Identity Database (NIDB). Subscribers can complete the linkage through multiple channels, such as USSD code (*996#), mobile apps, or in-person visits to network operator service centers. Each subscriber is permitted to have a maximum of four SIM cards per network operator, all of which must be linked to the same NIN. As of May 2025, approximately 172.67 million SIM cards have been successfully linked to NINs.

Title: Bank account opening
KeyTerms: Financial services, eKYC, AML/CFT
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - NIMC Verification service
Description: Digital ID verifies customer identities during bank account opening. The national identification number (NIN) stands as a primary identity verification instrument in financial customer onboarding backed by the Mandatory Use of the National Identification Number Regulations 2017. The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) circular of December 2023 mandates all financial institutions to integrate NIN and Bank Verification Number (BVN) into their know your customer (KYC) processes. These institutions include commercial, merchant, non-interest, and payment service banks, other financial institutions (OFIs), and mobile money operators. Under the tiered KYC framework, Tier 1 accounts require either BVN or NIN, while Tier 2 and Tier 3 accounts require both BVN and NIN. The NIN-based verification framework strengthens KYC and AML/CFT (Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism) compliance, and enables accurate customer profiling across Nigeria's banking and FinTech ecosystem.

Title: Taxpayer registration and tax compliance
KeyTerms: Tax registration, TIN, Revenue collection, eKYC
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: Digital ID verifies taxpayer identities during tax identification number (TIN) registration and ongoing tax compliance processes. In Nigeria, the national identification number (NIN) is one of the accepted identity verification instruments, alongside the Bank Verification Number (BVN) for TIN registration. Individuals can apply for a TIN online with their NIN or BVN. NIN is not explicitly mandatory for TIN issuance but serves as an important alternative to BVN, especially for individuals without bank accounts. The NIN-TIN linkage is part of Nigeria’s broader effort to harmonize taxpayer data across federal and state revenue authorities, connect banking and tax databases, and expand the tax net to capture informal sector participants. As of 2021, Nigeria had approximately 41 million registered taxpayers, though the exact proportion with NIN-linked TINs remains unclear.

Title: Education loan and student ID card
KeyTerms: Education, Scholarship, Loan
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: Digital ID verifies student identities and facilitates access to education loans through a national identification number (NIN)-linked biometric Government-to-People (G2P) cards. In March 2025, NIMC (National Identity Management Commission) and the Nigeria Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to roll out multi-purpose biometric student ID cards linked to the NIN. The cards feature multiple wallet capabilities, usable online and offline, with anti-counterfeiting measures that NIMC’s Director-General describes as impossible to forge or fake. Beyond loan disbursement, the biometric cards also enable loan tracking to ensure funds are used for their intended educational purposes and promote transparency and accountability in government-to-student transfers. NELFUND launched its loan portal in May 2024 and has since supported more than 437,000 students. NELFUND sought to register 1.2 million students by the end of 2025 through the NIN-linked student ID card.

Title: Employees compensation scheme
KeyTerms: Social insurance, Workforce verification, eKYC
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: Digital ID is being integrated to verify worker identities and streamline compensation claims under Nigeria’s Employee Compensation Scheme (ECS). The Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF) and the National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) signed an agreement in May 2025 to integrate the national identification number (NIN) database with enrolled workers’ data held under the ECS. The integration seeks to ease verification of workers’ biodata for compensation, improve the accuracy of employee compensation records, reduce fraudulent claims, and strengthen accountability across Nigeria’s workforce. NIN-based verification will enable the Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF) to seamlessly authenticate the identities of employees, employers, and claimants under the scheme. To date, NSITF has provided death benefits to more than 39,000 workers and disability and retirement benefits to 50,000 others.

Title: National social safety net program (cash transfers)
KeyTerms: Social protection, Social assistance, Conditional cash transfers
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - NIN-based biometric verification
Description: Digital ID verifies beneficiary in Nigeria’s National Social Safety Net Program, coordinated by the National Social Safety-Nets Coordinating Office (NASSCO) under the Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs. The National Social Register (NSR), built in collaboration with the World Bank, serves as Nigeria’s official database of poor and vulnerable households and is being integrated with the national identification number (NIN) to improve data accuracy, eliminate duplication, and ensure cash transfers reach legitimate beneficiaries. As of August 2025, approximately 7.9 million households had been visited and 10.2 million NINs collected, of which NIMC (National Identity Management Commission) successfully validated 9.6 million. By August 2025, at least 8.1 million households had received one or more tranches of NGN 25,000 cash transfers, paid directly into beneficiaries’ bank accounts or mobile wallets following NIN validation.

Title: Enrollment in national health insurance
KeyTerms: Health insurance, Social protection
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: Digital ID verifies the identities of citizens during enrollment in health insurance and service access in Nigeria. The National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA) Act, enacted in 2022, requires individuals to provide a National Identification Number (NIN) to enroll in any NHIA health insurance plan. New customers must submit their NIN through the NHIA self-service enrollment portal launched in September 2025, which allows them to enroll, manage their details, and access health insurance services online through their NIN, email, or phone number. The mandatory NIN requirement has improved transparency, accountability, and the integrity of enrollment data, reduced fraudulent registrations, and eliminated duplicate accounts. As of November 2025, NHIA coverage reached approximately 21 million Nigerians. The government targets 44 million customers by 2030 as part of Nigeria’s Universal Health Coverage (UHC) strategy.

Title: SIM registration using NIK number
KeyTerms: SIM registration,  e-KYC
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - Single-factor authentication (Demographic data is verified)
Description: In Indonesia, residents submit their Nomor Induk Kependudukan (NIK) and family card (KK) through SMS registration to their telecom operator, which then verifies the data against Dukcapil’s database through an API. The verification returns an instant Yes/No response. If matched, the SIM is activated; if not, the registration is rejected.

Title: Bank account opening using NIK and IKD
KeyTerms: Financial Inclusion, e-KYC, Know-Your-Customer, Customer onboarding, Digital Onboarding, Paperless Banking
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor Authentication (NIK Number and Face Verification)
Description: In Indonesia, residents can open a bank account either in person or remotely through the Identitas Kependudukan Digital (IKD) app. The app facilitates e-KYC through face verification with the resident’s Nomor Induk Kependudukan (NIK) number. Once the resident’s identity is successfully established, the verified details are shared with the bank.

Title: Accessing employment and labour benefits using NIK and IKD
KeyTerms: Social Security, Social Protection
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor Authentication (NIK Number and Face Verification)
Description: In Indonesia, the Nomor Induk Kependudukan (NIK) and Identitas Kependudukan Digital (IKD) app is used to access employment and labor benefits. NIK and IKD are used to verify beneficiaries’ identities during registration and deduplication, and to facilitate claims through Indonesia's Social Security Agency for the Employment Jamsostek Mobile (JMO) app. Beneficiaries complete face authentication, and the system performs 1:1 matching to confirm their identity. Upon successful authentication, beneficiaries can access employment and labor benefits.

Title: Access to pre-employment cash assistance using NIK
KeyTerms: Social Security, Social Protection, Employability, Upskilling
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor Authentication (NIK Number and Face Verification)
Description: The Indonesian government's pre-employment card program initiative offers cash assistance and online training to job seekers, laid-off workers, and those who seek to enhance their skills. Under this program, Nomor Induk Kependudukan (NIK)-based verification and facial authentication ensure secure, targeted enrollment and benefits disbursement during registration.

Title: Access to health app via NIK
KeyTerms: Health records, Appointments, Vaccination records
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor Authentication (NIK Number and Face Verification)
Description: In Indonesia, residents use their Nomor Induk Kependudukan (NIK) as a unique identifier to log in to the SATUSEHAT app, the official application of the Indonesian Ministry of Health. The system verifies the NIK against the national population database, and users authenticate themselves through face authentication. On successful verification, the app enables residents to access electronic medical records, track vaccinations, monitor health metrics, and manage medication.

Title: Accessing national health insurance via NIK
KeyTerms: Health Insurance, National Health Insurance
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor Authentication (NIK Number and Face Verification)
Description: In Indonesia, residents use their Nomor Induk Kependudukan (NIK) as the primary identifier to access the national health insurance program, Jaminan Kesehatan Nasional (JKN). NIK is used to confirm identity and eligibility to enroll and access services through the JKN app or at health facilities. Residents authenticate themselves through the JKN app, and upon successful authentication, they can access health insurance services, check membership status, and avail themselves of benefits.

Title: Scholarship application using NIK
KeyTerms: Scholarship, Education
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - Single Factor Authentication (NIK Number)
Description: The Nomor Induk Kependudukan (NIK) is required to apply for the Indonesia Lembaga Pengelola Dana Pendidikan (LPDP) state-funded scholarship. During registration, applicants enter their NIK to verify their identity against the national population database, also known as Dukcapil. This ensures that applicants' demographic details are accurate and prevent duplication or fraud during the selection process.

Title: Access to the conditional cash transfer using NIK
KeyTerms: Social Benefit, Financial Aid, Social Security
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - Single Factor Authentication (NIK Number)
Description: The Program Keluarga Harapan (PKH), Indonesian for Family Hope Program, is the country's largest conditional cash transfer initiative designed to reduce poverty and improve human capital. It provides quarterly financial assistance to low-income households. The Nomor Induk Kependudukan (NIK) of the family head is used for verification of households listed in the central database to determine social aid eligibility under PKH. Upon successful verification, the household is enrolled under PKH, and social assistance is disbursed through bank accounts or e-wallets linked to verified NIKs.

Title: Tax Filing using CPF and gov.br
KeyTerms: Income Tax Return, Tax Filing, Revenue and Taxation
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: The CPF or individual taxpayer registry serves as the unique taxpayer identifier in Brazil for all income tax–related services. Residents authenticate themselves through gov.br to access the tax portal; once authenticated, they can submit and file their income tax returns.

Title: Access to direct benefit transfer (in kind) using CPF/gov.br
KeyTerms: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), Social Security, Social Protection, Food Security, Food Distribution
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: The CPF is used to validate the beneficiary's eligibility and is cross-checked against the social registry. Beneficiaries authenticate themselves through gov.br; once authenticated, they can access their benefits.

Title: Access to direct benefit transfer (in cash) using CPF/gov.br
KeyTerms: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), Social Security, Social Protection
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: Direct benefit transfer (DBT) programs, such as Brazil’s Bolsa Família, are conditional cash transfer (CCT) programs that use the CPF as a unique identifier to cross-check beneficiaries against the unified social registry. Beneficiaries authenticate themselves through gov.br to access the cash transfers.

Title: Registration and updating of the social registry using CPF/gov.br
KeyTerms: Social Protection, Social registry
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: CPF is the mandatory identifier for individuals to register and update their information in the social registry. The Cadastro Único (CadÚnico), a social registry database, serves as a foundation for other social and labour protection programs. Residents authenticate themselves through the gov.br login to register and update their information.

Title: Access to the labour benefit account using gov.br
KeyTerms: Labour Benefits
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: The CPF serves as the unique identifier for the Fundo de Garantia do Tempo de Serviço (FGTS), which means the Length-of-Service Guarantee Fund, and other labour benefit accounts. Under the FGTS program, funds are credited to workers’ accounts, and withdrawals are carried out through the FGTS digital platform. Users authenticate themselves through gov.br, with the authentication assurance level based on the account type, namely gold, silver, or bronze.

Title: Access to vaccination records using gov.br
KeyTerms: Health Records, Vaccination Records, National Digital Health Platform
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: Gov.br is a standard authentication mechanism used to book and access vaccination records. Users can view and download their vaccination certificate by authenticating themselves through gov.br. The authentication factor varies depending on the account type.

Title: Access to the national digital health platform using CPF and gov.br
KeyTerms: Health Records, Vaccination Records, National Digital Health Platform
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: CPF serves as the primary unique ID to access the national digital health platform. It enables citizens to access their unified health record through the National Health Data Network (RNDS). The RNDS progressively connects public and private health providers; currently, more than 80% of Brazilian states and 68% of municipalities use RNDS data to organize health services and support public health planning.

Title: SIM issuance and activation using CPF and gov.br
KeyTerms: KYC, Electronic Know Your Customers (eKYC), SIM registration, Customer Onboarding
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: Brazil has more than 260 million active cellular lines, all tied to CPF records. The CPF serves as the unique identifier for SIM card activation. Authentication through gov.br credentials strengthens digital verification for new activations and portability requests. The customer initiates a SIM registration and activation request through the telecom service provider's app or website and verifies identity through gov.br. This ties the activation to the correct person and reduces risks, such as identity impersonation and fraudulent activations.

Title: Identity verification in competitive exams using gov.br and CPF/CIN
KeyTerms: Competitive exams, Staff Selection Commission
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: Candidates are required to present digital documents for identification exclusively through official applications accessed with their gov.br accounts. The gov.br account serves as the gateway to access digital documents, and it is of three types, namely bronze, silver, and gold. The higher the level, the more digital services citizens can access. Users can complete verification to upgrade their account level through facial authentication, validation with accredited bank accounts, or proof of identity on official channels.

Title: Higher education and scholarship registration using gov.br and CPF/CIN
KeyTerms: Education, Scholarship, Enrollment
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: Students in Brazil require a gov.br account to register for higher education admissions and to access the scholarship and student loan portal. They authenticate using CPF/CIN through the gov.br app or website, and the authentication assurance level varies based on account type, whether gold, silver, or bronze.

Title: Bank account opening using gov.br and CPF/CIN
KeyTerms: Finance, Financial Inclusion, e-KYC, Know-Your-Customer,  Customer onboarding, Digital Onboarding, Paperless Banking
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: The gov.br platform integrates with accredited banks to authenticate users for banking services. Partner banks allow customers to use their banking credentials to log in to gov.br. Customers initiate the process through the bank's app or website, authenticate it using gov.br, and then consent to share verified data with banks. By 2024, 14 of the largest banks in Brazil had integrated gov.br login for customer onboarding.

Title: Access to the digital school management system using e-ID (Smart-ID/Mobile-ID)
KeyTerms: e-School, Education, School Management, Student Records, Digital Education
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication (verification code and PIN1/PIN2)
Description: e-Kool is Estonia’s national digital school management platform that provides a unified digital interface for schools, teachers, students, and parents across the country. Users authenticate with their national digital ID and PIN1. This ensures secure, verified logins for all users. Once authenticated, teachers can record grades, attendance, and homework assignments. Students can view their timetables, grades, and upcoming lessons, while parents can monitor their child’s academic progress, communicate with teachers, and receive notifications from the school.

Title: Land and property transactions using e-ID (Smart-ID/Mobile-ID)
KeyTerms: e-Land Registry, Land Register, Property, Real Estate,  Land Ownership,  Digital Property Records
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication (verification code and PIN1/PIN2)
Description: In Estonia, the e-Land Registry is operated by the Centre of Registers and Information Systems (RIK) under the Ministry of Justice. It provides real-time, transparent access to land and property information with the national digital ID. Citizens, notaries, and legal professionals authenticate their identity using national digital ID credentials to access the land and property register. The portal provides updated information about land plots, which include ownership details, mortgages, and boundaries. This makes property due diligence entirely digital and paperless. Property transactions, such as transfers of ownership and creation of mortgages, are processed digitally. Notaries authenticate and sign documents using qualified electronic signatures, PIN2.

Title: Access to the agricultural registry and aid using e-ID (Smart-ID/Mobile-ID)
KeyTerms: e-PRIA, Agriculture, Agricultural Registry, Agricultural Aid, Farmer Registry, Animal Registry
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication (verification code and PIN1/PIN2)
Description:
In Estonia, e-PRIA is a digital portal for the Agricultural Registers and Information Board (ARIB). It enables farmers, landowners, and agricultural businesses to manage their interactions with national and the EU agricultural support programs entirely online. 
Users authenticate with their national digital ID credentials and personal identification number 1 (PIN1). After successful authentication, they can access the animal registry to manage and update records of livestock. They can also apply for national and EU agricultural aid and subsidies, track the status of their applications, and manage land use data linked to their farm holdings.

Title: Access to transport e-services using e-ID (Smart-ID/Mobile-ID)
KeyTerms: Driving License, Vehicle Registration, Digital Transport Services
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication (verification code and PIN1/PIN2)
Description:
The transport authority in Estonia offers a comprehensive suite of digital services accessible through the national digital ID. This allows residents to manage their transport-related administrative needs entirely online. Users authenticate to the transport administration e-service portal with their personal identification number 1 (PIN1).
On successful authentication, they can check the validity and details of their driving license, submit applications for new driving documents or renewals, and manage vehicle ownership and registration records. They can formalize vehicle ownership digitally and sign the transfer document with PIN2, which eliminates the need for physical presence at transport offices.

Title: Access to civil registration services using e-ID (Smart-ID/Mobile-ID)
KeyTerms: Civil Registration, Marriage Registration, Divorce Registration, Civil Status, Population Register, Digital Civil Services, Birth Registration, Death Registration
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication (verification code and PIN1/PIN2)
Description: In Estonia, civil registration services are available digitally, which include the registration of births, deaths, marriages, and divorces. Estonia digitalized marriage registration in 2022 and divorce registration in 2024, which completed Estonia's fully digital civil status service portfolio. Citizens authenticate with their national e-ID credentials. The population register maintains records of civil status events in real-time, with all submissions and approvals digitally signed using a second personal identification number 2 (PIN2).

Title: e-File and legal proceedings using e-ID (Smart-ID/Mobile-ID)
KeyTerms: e-File, Justice System, Court Services, Legal Proceedings,  Digital Court
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication (verification code and PIN1/PIN2)
Description: The e-File system in Estonia, operated by the Ministry of Justice, enables full digital participation in civil, administrative, and criminal court proceedings. All parties to a legal case, residents, lawyers, prosecutors, and court officials, authenticate to the e-File portal through their digital ID credentials. On successful authentication, lawyers can electronically submit pleadings, evidence, and other court documents, and parties can monitor the real-time progress of their case and receive notifications of court decisions and deadlines. All submitted documents are digitally signed with a personal identification number 2 (PIN2), which creates legally binding qualified electronic signatures. The e-File system operates 24/7, which allows legal actions to be filed outside traditional office hours.

Title: e-signing document and attestation using e-ID (Smart-ID/Mobile-ID)
KeyTerms: Digital Signature, Qualified Electronic Signature (QES),  Document Signing,  Electronic Signature
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication (verification code and PIN1/PIN2)
Description: In Estonia, citizens, businesses, and government agencies sign documents and contracts digitally with full legal validity. They use their e-ID, mobile-ID, or smart-ID to create a qualified electronic signature (QES). A QES has the same legal value as a handwritten signature. The user enters the personal identification number 2 (PIN2) on their device to sign. This action triggers the secure cryptographic process. The system then adds a timestamp and a certificate chain to the document, which makes it tamper-evident and easy to verify. In Estonia, digital signatures are in use across almost every sector, which includes government approvals, bank authorizations, real estate transactions, healthcare consent, and private contracts, among others.

Title: Access to labour and social benefits using e-ID (Smart-ID/Mobile-ID)
KeyTerms: Social Insurance, Pension, Disability Benefits, Parental Leave, Family Benefits, Social Security
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication (verification code and PIN1/PIN2)
Description: The Estonian Social Insurance Board (ENSIB) provides a wide range of labour and social benefit services accessible through the national state portal with e-ID.  Residents authenticate themselves through a personal identification number (PIN1) to access their personal social insurance dashboard. Residents can apply for pensions, disability benefits, parental leave, maternity benefits, and other family support programs. They digitally sign applications with PIN2, which creates legally binding qualified electronic signatures.

Title: Access to unemployment insurance services using e-ID (Smart-ID/Mobile-ID)
KeyTerms: Unemployment Benefits, Social Protection, Employment Services, Welfare
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication (code verification and PIN1/PIN2)
Description: The Estonian Unemployment Insurance Fund (Eesti Töötukassa) operates a fully digital service portal that allows Estonian residents to access employment and unemployment services entirely online through their national electronic ID. Citizens authenticate with their personal identification number (PIN1). Once logged in, residents can register as unemployed, browse available job offers that match their profile, apply for unemployment benefits and allowances, manage their benefit claims, and track payment history. The digital ID layer ensures benefit applications are securely linked to verified individual identities. This prevents fraudulent claims and supports precise eligibility assessment.

Title: Bank account opening using e-ID (Smart-ID/Mobile-ID)
KeyTerms: Financial Inclusion, Digital Onboarding, Online Banking, e-KYC
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication (code verification and PIN1/PIN2)
Description: Banks in Estonia allow digital onboarding and day-to-day online banking operations through the national digital ID. Residents authenticate themselves on bank portals and mobile apps using their credentials through personal identification number (PIN1). Upon successful authentication, electronic know your customer (e-KYC) details are shared with banks. For online transactions, fund transfers, and high-value operations, residents authorize these using the PIN2 digital signature, which meets the legal requirements of qualified electronic signatures.

Title: Tax filing using e-ID (Mobile-ID/Smart-ID)
KeyTerms: e-Tax, Tax Filing, Income Tax, Tax Return
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication (verification code and PIN1/PIN2)
Description: In Estonia, residents can file their tax return online with their national digital ID. Residents authenticate themselves on the e-tax portal through a verification code and their personal identification number (PIN1). After successful authentication and login, the portal automatically pre-fills tax return details, such as income and withholding. The system collects this data from employers, banks, and government registries and retrieves it through the X-Road platform. This follows the once-only principle, which ensures residents do not have to submit the same data again. Residents can review the pre-filled information, make any corrections, and submit their declaration by signing with PIN2 to create a qualified electronic signature.

Title: i-Voting (Online Voting) via e-ID (Mobile-ID/Smart-ID)
KeyTerms: i-Voting,  Online Voting, Electoral System, National Electoral Committee
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication (code verification and PIN1/PIN2)
Description: Estonia was the first country to conduct legally binding national elections over the internet, a system introduced in 2005. It allows eligible voters anywhere in the world to cast their ballot securely with their national e-ID credentials. Voters authenticate themselves through the first personal identification number (PIN1), and the actual vote is digitally signed with PIN2, which generates a qualified electronic signature. The cryptographic process ensures end-to-end integrity and non-repudiation, while anonymity is preserved through vote encryption and the separation of identity from ballot content. The Population Register validates voter eligibility in real time through secure interoperability services.

Title: Access to the health insurance fund via e-ID (Mobile-ID/Smart-ID)
KeyTerms: Health Insurance,  Health Portal,  Digital Health Insurance
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication (verification code and PIN1/PIN2)
Description: The Estonian Health Insurance Fund (EHIF) enables residents to manage their health insurance services digitally through the national health portal. Residents authenticate themselves through the verification code and personal identification number (PIN1) to access a personalized health insurance dashboard. On successful authentication, the user can access services once the validity of health insurance coverage is verified. They can also view the medical bill history paid by the fund, check reimbursement status for medicines and procedures, and review the electronic health record summary.

Title: e-Prescriptions using e-ID (Mobile-ID/Smart-ID)
KeyTerms: e-Health, e-Prescriptions, Healthcare Access, Digital Health
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication (verification code and PIN1/PIN2)
Description: e-Prescription is a nationwide digital prescription system that allows doctors to issue, write, and sign prescriptions electronically with their e-ID. It also enables pharmacies to dispense medicines through the patient’s digital ID. The system stores the prescription in the national e-Health database and links it to the patient’s personal ID number. A resident can collect medicine by showing their e-ID at the pharmacy. The pharmacist accesses the prescription from the central system through the resident’s ID number and dispenses the medicine.

Title: Access to health records using e-ID (Mobile-ID/Smart-ID)
KeyTerms: e-Health, Electronic Health Records, Healthcare Access, Digital Health
