AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication (verification code and PIN1/PIN2)
Description: In Estonia, residents can securely access and manage their personal health records with the national e-ID (Mobile-ID, or Smart-ID), through the Estonian Health Information System (EHIS). Residents authenticate themselves through a verification code and personal identification number (PIN1). On successful authentication, residents can view their electronic health records, check past consultations, view prescribed medicines, and access vaccination histories.

Title: Issuance of Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) using NID verification
KeyTerms: Taxpayer ID, Tax Registration, Revenue, Digital Services
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - NID-based demographic verification
Description: Bangladesh's National Board of Revenue (NBR) uses the national ID (NID) as the primary identity credential for issuing taxpayer identification numbers (TINs). All TINs issued in Bangladesh are connected with the applicant's NID. TIN registration is accessible online and allows citizens to apply by providing their NID, which is verified through a demographic verification API call to the Bangladesh Election Commission.

Title: Registration for SIM using NID
KeyTerms: SIM Registration, Telecom, e-KYC, Digital Onboarding
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - NID-based demographic and biometric verification
Description: The Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) mandates biometric verification using national ID (NID) for all SIM card registrations in the country. The registration process requires citizens to present their NID at a telecom operator's outlet or authorized agent outlets, where their fingerprint is captured and matched against the NID biometric database managed by the Bangladesh Election Commission.

Title: Opening of agent bank account using NID
KeyTerms: Financial Inclusion, Agent Banking, e-KYC,  Digital Banking, Account Opening
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: Agent banking operators in Bangladesh use national ID (NID)-based e-KYC for agent bank account opening. Agent banking extends formal financial services to rural and semi-urban areas through authorized agents, and NID-based e-KYC is central to enabling this model. The account opening process involves NID demographic verification through an API provided by the Bangladesh Election Commission, supplemented by OTP managed by the provider.

Title: Opening of Mobile Financial Services (MFS) account using NID
KeyTerms: Financial Inclusion, MFS, e-KYC,  Account Opening, Digital Onboarding
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: Bangladesh Bank, in collaboration with mobile financial service (MFS) operators such as bKash and Nagad, uses national ID (NID) and birth registration number (BRN)-based electronic Know Your Customer (e-KYC) for digital account opening. The e-KYC process for MFS account opening involves NID and BRN demographic verification through an API call to the Bangladesh Election Commission, supplemented by OTP authentication, managed by the MFS provider or the Ministry of Finance. The NID-based e-KYC system has significantly reduced the time and cost of onboarding new users, which eliminates the need for physical document submission and in-person verification in many cases.

Title: Creation of shared health record (SHR) using NID
KeyTerms: Health, Shared Health Record, Health ID, Health Information Exchange, Digital Health
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - NID-based demographic verification
Description: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in Bangladesh is developing a shared health Record (SHR) system as part of its broader health information exchange (HIE) initiative. The system assigns a unique health ID to each citizen, built on top of the existing national ID (NID) or birth registration number (BRN). Health ID serves as a universal patient identifier that enables authorized healthcare providers to access and share a patient’s clinical history across different facilities. Citizens register using their NID or BRN, with their NID credentials verified through demographic verification APIs provided by the Bangladesh Election Commission.

Title: Registration for vaccination using NID/BRN
KeyTerms: Health, COVID-19, Vaccination, NID, Immunisation, Digital Health
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: Surokkha app is the primary digital platform for COVID-19 vaccination registration in Bangladesh. The app uses national ID (NID) or birth registration number (BRN) to register citizens. NID credentials are verified through a demographic verification API call to the Bangladesh Election Commission , while BRN verification is handled through the Office of the Registrar General. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare also sent OTPs during the registration process to add a layer of security. Once registered and verified, citizens received vaccination slots at designated centers, and their vaccination status was digitally recorded.

Title: Access to Fisherman ID and DBT benefits using NID
KeyTerms: Agriculture, Fisheries, Fisher ID, Direct Benefit Transfer, G2P
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: The Sustainable Coastal and Marine Fisheries Program, administered by the Ministry of Fisheries and Livestock, uses the national ID (NID) as the primary identity credential to register fishermen and deliver cash benefits. Fishermen register using their NID to receive a Fisherman Card. The NID is verified through a demographic verification API provided by the Bangladesh Election Commission. Benefits are disbursed directly to the registered beneficiaries through NID-linked mobile financial services (MFS).

Title: Disbursement of agriculture subsidies using NID
KeyTerms: Agriculture, Subsidy, Direct Benefit Transfer, DBT, Mobile Financial Services, G2P
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: N/A
Description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Bangladesh, uses the national ID (NID) system to onboard farmers as beneficiaries for agricultural subsidies and deliver cash transfers through NID-enabled mobile financial services (MFS). NID serves as the primary identity credential for farmer registration, with NID numbers verified through a demographic API call to the Bangladesh Election Commission. Once registered, benefits are transferred directly to farmers' NID-linked MFS wallets, such as bKash or Nagad.

Title: Provision of primary education stipend using NID/BRN
KeyTerms: Education, Stipend, Scholarship, School Enrollment
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - BRN-based demographic verification
Description: The Primary Education Stipend Program (PESP) is one of Bangladesh's oldest and largest direct benefit transfer initiatives in the education sector. The program provides a monthly stipend to mothers of primary school students. Beneficiary enrollment is based on BRN-linked unique IDs (UIDs) assigned to students. Verification of beneficiaries is conducted through the Single Registry using the birth registration number (BRN) of the student and the national ID (NID) of their mother. NID verification is performed through the demographic verification API provided by the Bangladesh Election Commission, while BRN verification is handled through the office of the Registrar General.

Title: Digital voter registration and a hybrid election using a national digital ID
KeyTerms: Elections, civic participation, voter registration, biometric verification, data exchange, digital inclusion, accessibility, offline authentication
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication for election officials and digital systems
Description:
Papua New Guinea faces gaps in voter registration and election processes. Identity data remains fragmented. Voter rolls often contain duplicate or missing records. Remote communities struggle to access registration or update services. These gaps reduce trust in election results.

This use case proposes a hybrid election system. It integrates SevisPass Digital ID, the SevisDEx data exchange platform, and National ID (NID) with census data and eKYC processes. The system establishes verified voter identities across the entire voting population. The system integrates online authentication via SevisPass and offline voter registration by election agents. 

This approach reduces duplicate and inflated rolls by linking identities through biometrics and probabilistic matching, creating single, verified voter records. It speeds up voter enrollment processes and reduces costs as it enables consent-based, auditable data exchange for eligibility checks. Further developing the manual paper-based election process can transition to electronic devices, such as voting machines.

Title: Access to loans, subsidies, and insurance by farmers using the national digital ID
KeyTerms: Agriculture, digital inclusion, accessibility, regional integration, blockchain, IoT sensors, subsidy management, food security
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication at Smart Village Hubs and digital platform access for resource applications
Description:
Farmers in Southern Africa lack reliable identity systems and accurate land records. This limits their access to subsidies, loans, and insurance. Fraudulent claims divert resources, and farmers struggle to manage climate and price risks.

This use case proposes a digital farmer ID to track financial support for farmers in one place. A digital farmer ID is assigned to each farmer, which provides a unique biometric identity using fingerprints or facial recognition. The system links this ID to a central farmer registry. The database stores key details such as land size, crops, livestock, water use, and yield history.

Based on these verified details, the government and other financial institutions provide support to farmers. The system simplifies access to subsidies, credit, and insurance. It also connects farmers with buyers and cooperatives.

Title: Tax compliance system using a national digital ID
KeyTerms: Public finance, governance, tax administration, fraud prevention, financial data integration, blockchain, AI-driven audits
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 3 - Multi-factor biometric authentication for tax authority access and financial data verification
Description:
Senegal loses 526.4 billion FCFA each year to tax evasion, equivalent to 3.4% of GDP. Most businesses operate informally, and only 6.5% register under the National Identification Number for Companies and Associations (NINEA). Weak enforcement and poor taxpayer verification allow fraud and reduce public investments.

This use case proposes a system that integrates the national digital ID with the NINEA taxpayer system and the financial database. The system mandates biometric verification using digital IDs to confirm business owners and prevent duplicate or fraudulent identities. 

The system verifies taxpayers in real time and supports AI-based audits to detect false declarations. It allows secure data-sharing between tax authorities, banks, customs, and registries. The integration of digital payments and electronic invoicing ensures transaction traceability.

Title: Property ownership and transfer management using a national digital ID
KeyTerms: Public services, property management, blockchain, smart contracts, fraud prevention, asset security
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 3 - Hardware and cryptographic-based authentication for property transfer transactions using blockchain
Description:
Property ownership and transfer process in Eastern Africa remain complex and prone to fraud. This makes transactions insecure and reduces trust.

The proposed use case uses a national digital ID to simplify property management. It links digital IDs with property records to verify ownership and prevent fraud.

The platform allows users to list and sell properties. Buyers can verify ownership before they initiate a transaction. It records every transaction on a tamper-proof blockchain ledger. This creates a clear property history for audits and legal use.

Title: Verification of academic records using a national digital ID
KeyTerms: Education, employment, public administration, fraud prevention, credential verification, AI-powered matching, real-time data management
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication for job seeker and employer access to verified credential systems
Description:
A study in West Africa shows that 68% of CVs mislead employers and 29% list incorrect qualifications. This raises hiring costs and slows the hiring process.

The proposed use case provides a digital ID-based platform for employment records. Individuals seeking employment create profiles on the platform and upload their original certificates.

The platform verifies qualifications through diploma/degree-issuing authorities and skills agencies, then generates trusted digital profiles. Employers post jobs on the platform and receive verified applications. The government uses the data to plan employment policies and target social support.

Title: Access to youth entrepreneurship support using the national digital ID
KeyTerms: Entrepreneurship, financial services, financial inclusion, digital inclusion & accessibility, mentorship, blockchain, AI-driven recommendations
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication for loan applications and financial transactions
Description:
Young entrepreneurs in Eastern Africa face barriers to finance, mentorship, and business networks. The absence of formal identification prevents them from opening bank accounts and securing loans.
 
This use case proposes a digital platform that uses a national digital ID to bridge these gaps. Entrepreneurs create their profile on the platform. These profiles show their skills, business ideas, and financial history. This helps them access microloans, crowdfunding, and grants, as this platform showcases their financial performance.

The platform will also offer online courses, mentorship, and networking opportunities, thereby facilitating skill development and business growth.

Title: Access to emergency response using the national digital ID
KeyTerms: AI-enabled emergency response system
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication for emergency alert triggering and emergency services dashboard access
Description:
Senegal experiences significant emergency service delays. It is mainly due to communication gaps, poor location tracking, and weak case prioritization. Studies show that effective emergency management could prevent up to 36% of disabilities and 45% of deaths.

The proposed use case idea suggests a platform to improve response efficiency through a national digital ID and AI. Users can authenticate through their MOSIP-backed national digital ID and select the required service, such as police, medical, or fire support. The system shares the user’s location automatically with responders.

AI-based bots guide users with first-aid steps while they await emergency responders. Users can track response status in real time. The platform also supports direct communication through chat. This platform reduces reliance on verbal descriptions, improves resource allocation, and shortens response time.

Title: Creation of a digital medical identity and access to health records using the national digital ID
KeyTerms: Healthcare, digital health records, patient identity, interoperability, mobile access
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication for healthcare providers to access patient medical files
Description:
Countries in the West and Central Africa region face inconsistencies with healthcare digitalization. People also do not have a digital medical identity. This causes treatment delays and proliferation/loss of physical medical documents.

The proposed use case will develop a mobile application that creates a unique digital medical identity for each patient. It stores medical records in a centralized place, and patients can securely access their medical history online.

Each patient’s medical identity is linked to their unique national digital ID. The linked medical records are accessible through a secure QR code. 
The system syncs electronic medical records regularly across healthcare facilities. It also enables data exchange between healthcare providers. Patients can control access to their medical information.

Title: Targeted agricultural subsidy delivery using national digital ID
KeyTerms: Agriculture, fraud prevention, data-driven decision making, machine learning, digital identity, subsidy management, food security, elite capture
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication for subsidy program access and benefit verification
Description:
Sub-Saharan African governments face challenges such as subsidy fraud, elite capture, and non-targeted allocation. This causes an adverse impact on food security and poverty reduction.

This use case proposes the use of a national digital ID-based single sign-on to verify the farmer’s identity. This will help eliminate ghost beneficiaries through secure digital identity verification, preventing fraud and misallocation. Machine learning algorithms will analyse farmer data to accurately identify and prioritise vulnerable populations for subsidy distribution. The system ensures transparent, auditable subsidy allocation processes.

Title: Voting using a national digital ID
KeyTerms: Public services, civic participation, biometric authentication, electoral security, blockchain, accessibility, fraud prevention
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 3 - Hardware-based biometric fingerprint authentication combined with digital card verification at polling stations
Description:
West African elections face serious challenges. Instances of fraud, such as multiple voting and ballot stuffing, remain common. Rural and disabled voters often face exclusion.
 
The use case proposes to integrate national identity cards, known as Carte Nationale d'Identité (CNI), and fingerprint biometrics for voter verification at digital polling stations. Each voter inserts the card for initial verification and then scans their fingerprints for confirmation. Once verified, the voter selects a candidate through a simple interface. The system encrypts each vote and stores it on a blockchain.

Title: Access to the patient's health records and digital prescriptions using the national digital ID
KeyTerms: Healthcare, cybersecurity, privacy & data protection, biometric authentication, blockchain, prescription security
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication for healthcare providers accessing prescription systems
Description:
Malawi's healthcare system faces critical challenges such as prescription fraud, medication errors, and fragmented health records.

This use case proposes blockchain-powered prescription records. It gives real-time access to authorized users. The system links the digital IDs of patients and healthcare providers to their respective profiles. 

Healthcare providers link each prescription to a verified patient profile through digital ID, which pharmacies can verify at the point of service. The system ensures prescriptions cannot be altered without detection. Privacy is preserved through permissioned access controls. The system is designed to scale across Malawi’s healthcare network as adoption grows.

Title: Student loan auto-repayment via national digital ID and tax integration
KeyTerms: Education, financial services, social protection, data exchange, employment verification, automated workflows
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - System-level authentication for government agency data exchange via tax records
Description:
Botswana’s student loan system is based on manual checks. Repayment of the loan is also tracked manually. This leads to missed repayments and limits funds for new scholarships. There is no reliable way to determine the employment status or to request repayment. 

The use case proposes to link Botswana’s Unified Services Digital ID (BoSDID) to tax identification numbers (TINs). It uses data from the Botswana Unified Revenue Service (BURS) to track employment status. The system detects when a graduate is employed and triggers their loan repayment automatically. The system uses real-time tax data and removes the need for self-reporting.

Title: Airport check-in using national digital ID
KeyTerms: Transportation & logistics, border security, biometric authentication, facial recognition, accessibility, speed optimization
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Hardware-based facial biometric authentication
Description:
Airports in Morocco face delays of 15-30 minutes at passport checking points. Manual photo checks create errors, which leads to confusion for both travellers and staff.

This use case proposes the use of facial authentication linked to a digital ID. The system would replace manual checks, improve accuracy, reduce errors, and speed up passenger flow.

Title: Police clearance using the national digital ID
KeyTerms: Public services, law enforcement, biometric authentication, facial recognition, digital verification, cybersecurity, accessibility
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication
Description:
PNG citizens face delays when they apply for police clearance. The process requires NID numbers, facial photos, and in-person fingerprint collection. Applicants must visit the National Crime Records Office, which increases cost and travel time. In some provinces, the process takes up to three weeks.

The proposed smart police clearance portal simplifies this process through SevisPass. Citizens log in with the SevisPass single sign-on, and the system fills registration forms with identity data that has been verified.

Users pay online and submit facial scans through SevisPass. The system matches these scans with government-verified identity records. This removes the need to collect fingerprints on-site. Citizens complete the process through their phone or their computer camera.

Title: Access to public and private service delivery using the national digital ID
KeyTerms: Public services, service delivery, digital access portal, biometric authentication, rural accessibility, data sharing, interoperability
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication to access the service portal
Description:
Many citizens in PNG struggle to access essential services because identity checks are unreliable. Records remain fragmented, and manual processes create long queues and repeated registrations. Rural citizens are particularly affected, as they have to travel long distances and carry physical documents that are easy to lose or damage.

This use case proposes a unified digital platform built on SevisPass to streamline service delivery across government agencies and businesses. Citizens authenticate through biometrics-based ID checks and consent-based data sharing on a web and mobile interface.
With a verified SevisPass ID, users can access permits, personal records, appointments, social support, and work or financial services.

Title: e-KYC using a national digital ID to access financial services
KeyTerms: Financial services, digital payments, financial inclusion, biometric authentication, NFC cards, POS terminal, eKYC, AML compliance
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor authentication that combines biometrics and digital credentials for wallet access and transactions
Description:
About 75% of adults in PNG don’t have bank access because they lack a verifiable identity. Birth certificate coverage remains as low as 13%, which worsens exclusion.

This use case proposes a platform that integrates SevisPass to verify identity and fulfill KYC requirements when the citizen opens their account. SevisPass provides verified and portable identities, so users can confirm their identity without physical documents.

Users log in to the platform through multi-factor authentication to access their bank accounts securely. The system verifies national IDs, biometrics, and supporting documents. After authentication, users can access payments, merchant services, savings, and tokenized assets. Businesses benefit from reduced onboarding costs, while rural communities gain access to essential financial services.

Title: Access to a digital marketplace by farmers using a national digital ID
KeyTerms: Agriculture, digital marketplace, farmer verification, e-commerce, mobile-first, SMS/USSD, financial inclusion, digital inclusion
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - Single-factor authentication to access the farmer platform and basic transactions via USSD
Description:
PNG farmers lack verified identities and rely on feature phones. Internet access remains limited and prevents farmers from using digital platforms to stay updated on market trends. Buyers also struggle to find trusted suppliers.

This proposed platform connects farmers and buyers through a secure system. Farmers register with SevisPass, which verifies identity and removes false listings. In low-connectivity areas, community agents collect farmer data offline and sync it once connectivity is restored. Buyers use the platform’s website or app to view structured produce data, which they can filter by location, crop, quantity, availability, and price.

Buyers contact farmers through SMS or phone calls. Payments go directly to the farmers’ bank accounts via SevisWallet.

Title: Access to financial services using a national digital ID
KeyTerms: Financial services, digital identity, fraud prevention, loan processing, financial inclusion, biometric authentication, payments
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor authentication for loan applications and financial transactions
Description:
PNG has low financial inclusion as institutions follow manual verification to provide financial services. Citizens and businesses face fraud and delays as a result of it.

This use case proposes a secure digital ecosystem to address these challenges. The ecosystem includes mobile apps, institutional portals, and API integration. Users create digital profiles using the SevisPass-based biometric verification system. Banks send requests through the bank portal, and users approve data sharing via mobile applications. Verified data enables access to formal credit and lead to financial inclusion.

Title: Access to a centralized medical database of patients using a national digital ID
KeyTerms: Healthcare, digital health records, patient identity, data interoperability, medical continuity, cloud infrastructure, real-time access
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor biometric and authentication for healthcare provider access to patient records
Description:
PNG’s healthcare system relies on paper-based patient records. This leads to delays, repeated tests, and diagnostic errors due to loss and damage of these records.

The use case proposes a secure, cloud-based central repository. It stores patient medical histories, lab results, prescriptions, immunizations, and hospital visit records. Healthcare providers and patients access the system via SevisPass, which uses multifactor authentication. When a patient visits a facility, staff retrieve health data in real time after authentication. 
Patients can also view their records, test results, and appointments through the user portal. SevisDEx enables data exchange across facilities and ensures interoperability across PNG’s healthcare system.

Title: Access to telemedicine services by using the national digital ID
KeyTerms: Healthcare, telemedicine, digital consultations, rural access, price transparency, e-prescriptions, mobile device, digital inclusion
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication for healthcare provider access
Description:
Papua New Guinea faces major gaps in healthcare access. Rural communities lack doctors and facilities. Around 87% of rural communities lack regular access to a doctor, with only one doctor per 10,000 people in these areas. Rural residents must travel long distances for basic care.

This use case proposes a national telemedicine platform. Patients consult SevisPass-verified doctors via secure digital channels. The national healthcare authority onboards doctors onto the platform based on their verified qualifications. Patients can book online appointments for a reasonable fee. Doctors issue digitally signed prescriptions that patients can store in SevisWallet and share at the pharmacy through QR codes. The system sends medication reminders linked to patient IDs.

SevisDEx enables secure, consent-based sharing of medical records.  The platform also shows nearby verified clinics and facilitates emergency ambulance requests with location and identity details.

Title: Farmer verification and agricultural grant disbursal using a national digital ID
KeyTerms: Agriculture, rural development, project accountability, farmer verification, financial inclusion, data sharing, transparency
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - Single-factor authentication acceptable for farmer project participation checkpoints
Description:
Farmers in Papua New Guinea often have limited access to agricultural extension services and support mechanisms. In addition, agricultural grant and development programs face challenges related to the verification of beneficiary identities. Fake farmer profiles also lead to the misuse of the grants. 

This use case proposes using SevisPass to verify farmers and projects. Farmers give consent and confirm their identity before they submit proposals. After approval, the system records each farmer’s participation through identity check-ins. Final verification confirms project completion and real farmer involvement.

This approach blocks fake applications, flags suspicious projects, and improves transparency and accountability in public spending. Communities can track projects and ask local custodians questions.

Title: Social media account’s identity verification using the national digital ID
KeyTerms: Public services, cybersecurity, digital safety, anti-fraud, account verification, social media security, privacy & data protection, digital inclusion
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor authentication through Sevis PNG for all social media account creation and access
Description:
Papua New Guinea faces growing digital safety challenges, such as fake profiles, identity fraud, and online harassment, which are difficult to address because social media platforms do not have reliable user verification mechanisms. Women and public figures face harassment from anonymous or unverified accounts.

This use case proposes SevisPass as the national identity layer for all social media platforms. Users must verify their identity via OTP-based verification of the SevisPass digital ID when they activate an account. Users must verify their existing account. The system uses SevisPass for authentication and SevisDEx for secure verification and real-time checks.

This approach removes fake and anonymous accounts, which creates a safer online environment. The Department of Information and Communications Technology can monitor activity without exposing personal data.

Title: Access to verified digital education credentials using a national digital ID
KeyTerms: Education, digital credentials, teacher verification, workforce development, certificate authenticity, interoperability, data sharing, fraud prevention
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor authentication for school administrators and educators
Description:
Papua New Guinea faces challenges in verifying the authenticity of educational certificates. This prevents students from applying for scholarships in time and delays their entry into higher education. Paper-based systems cause lost transcripts, slow verification, and inconsistent national data. 

This use case proposes a platform that establishes a lifelong digital education identity that links every student and teacher. Each student and teacher is verified through their SevisPass IDs throughout their educational journey. Students receive digital credentials that are instantly shareable with schools, scholarship boards, and employers. All educational verifications occur exclusively through SevisPass, replacing paper-based methods. 

After graduation, verified educational records automatically link to a national employment hub, creating a transparent pathway from learning to employment. This integrated approach prevents fraud, ensures data accuracy, improves workforce readiness, and establishes PNG’s fully verified education-to-employment ecosystem.

Title: Maternal healthcare support to healthcare workers using the national digital ID
KeyTerms: Maternal health, rural health systems, health worker support, offline resources, digital inclusion, community health, training & development
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - Single-factor authentication acceptable for healthcare workers accessing offline maternal care resources
Description:
Papua New Guinea’s geography and dispersed population make maternal healthcare difficult in rural areas. Health workers often lack training and real-time support, and struggle to access medical guidance due to poor connectivity.

This use case proposes a maternal care support system with SevisPass Digital ID authentication. Verified health workers can log in, access maternal care resources, and record patient outcomes and share updates with provincial hospitals. Authorities can track key health indicators and monitor rural centers.

Title: Digital diploma credentials issuance and verification system using national digital ID
KeyTerms: Digital credentials, certificate issuance, public key infrastructure, verifiable credentials, data exchange, credential verification, digital inclusion
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - Students can present this digital diploma to an employer via Sevis PNG DPI ecosystem
Description:
Papua New Guinea faces challenges in verifying the authenticity of educational certificates. These challenges can affect employer confidence and reduce trust in academic credentials. The Department of Education and tertiary institutions currently do not have access to secure digital systems for issuing tamper-proof diploma certificates.

The proposed use case is a business-to-government (B2G) software system designed to address this problem. This system will enable educational institutions to issue digital credentials directly to students’ official SevisPass wallets. The platform serves as a secure backend and enables institutions to act as trusted issuers within the SevisPass ecosystem.

The workflow operates as follows: A registrar at a tertiary institution, or in the Department of Education, logs in with secure credentials and accesses student records to start credential issuance. After graduation, the registrar selects “Issue digital diploma.” The system creates a digitally signed credential and sends it through SevisDEx to the student’s SevisPass wallet. Employers can verify the diploma's authenticity instantly using their credentials through this system.

Title: Education certificate verification system using national digital ID
KeyTerms: Student identity, certificate verification, credential security, digital certification, QR code authentication, fraud prevention, public key infrastructure (PKI)
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - PKI-based authentication using SevisPass ID for school administrators and organizations accessing student records
Description:
Papua New Guinea relies on paper-based student registration and manual data entry, which creates errors such as misspelled names and inconsistent records. Schools also struggle to confirm student identity, and certificates can easily be edited and reproduced by anyone. Verification depends on manual checks, which are time-consuming and difficult to detect fraud.

This use case proposes a comprehensive national student identity system that will use SevisPass Digital ID, linked to the SevisDEx data exchange platform. Schools register students through a parent-assisted online registration portal or a dedicated school-based registration station to ensure each student has a verified identity before school certificate exams. 

The National Department of Education will issue passing certificates with a QR code linked to a digitally signed record using its public key infrastructure (PKI). Any registered organization can scan the QR code and verify student details using PKI certificates. Through this verification process, the verifying organization confirms the authenticity of the student’s name, school, year, and examination result.

Title: Emergency response and public safety reporting using a national digital ID
KeyTerms: Public safety, crime prevention, community security, real-time alerts, GPS location, data sharing, digital inclusion, privacy and data protection
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 0 - No verification needed for accessing emergency services and location data sharing, just pressing the panic button will activate the emergency response services
Description:
Certain regions of Papua New Guinea face public safety issues.  Slow emergency response and lack of a reliable online incident reporting platform worsen the issue. Women and young people face a higher risk.

The proposed mobile application will provide emergency support and act as a reporting platform. It would integrate SevisPass digital ID to verify individuals and create their profiles with emergency details. The system confirms identity during registration and login through biometric checks. This step prevents fake accounts and reduces false alerts.

When the emergency button on the app is activated, the app overrides the device’s usual phone settings to capture live audio and location. It sends this data to emergency responders, along with the user’s verified identity details. 

The system shares only the minimum required information, protecting sensitive data. Users maintain one trusted identity across services such as reporting, safety updates, and emergency support.

Title: Driver verification and real-time bus tracking using national digital ID
KeyTerms: Driver verification, fleet management, safety, real-time tracking, mobile device, community engagement
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor authentication for vehicle owner and driver  for safety and tracking
Description:
Papua New Guinea faces safety and accountability issues in the public motor vehicle (PMV) sector. Many buses run without proper permits or in unsafe conditions. This puts passengers and others at risk. Owners also struggle with theft, misuse, and poor service due to limited monitoring.

The digital PMV system use case proposes SevisPass digital ID to verify driver identities and link them to the public vehicle that they are assigned to operate. Each vehicle will have an ownership and maintenance record stored in a digital profile, linked to the owner's SevisPass ID. The driver will confirm their identity through multifactor authentication before they operate a vehicle.

The system tracks buses in real time through GPS, allowing owners to monitor their locations and driving behaviour. The system allows passengers to verify the driver by scanning the QR code on the vehicle’s exterior, which links to a real-time status page for the authenticated driver. Passengers can also send SMS alerts to report safety concerns. This system improves transparency and safety across the sector.

Title: Tracking child tuberculosis treatment adherence using national digital ID
KeyTerms: TB management, child health, social protection, digital inclusion, incentive management, data sharing, contact tracing
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - OTP-based authentication for verification and sharing of data with healthcare workers
Description:
The World Health Organisation classifies Papua New Guinea as a high-burden tuberculosis country. Children account for about 26% of reported cases. Many of these patients stop treatment due to stigma and social barriers. As a result, “lost-to-follow-up” cases continue to spread TB.

This use case proposes to use SevisPass and Sevis Wallet to solve this problem. When a child visits a clinic, staff verify the child’s identity through SevisPass and link the child's medical records to their SevisPass profile using the Medical Record Number (MRN). After this, every test, treatment decision, and visit to a healthcare center can be tracked via the child's SevisPass.

Health workers track adherence through regular check-ins. If a child misses any check-ins, workers respond quickly and trace them. When mandatory visits are completed, the system transfers incentives to caregivers through linked bank accounts. This approach can improve outcomes for nearly 400,000 children in Papua New Guinea.

Title: Access to a unified digital health record platform using a national digital ID
KeyTerms: Healthcare, digital health records, patient identity, USSD, SMS, offline-ready, data sharing, interoperability, rural access
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication for clinician and administrator access to health records (ID and OTP)
Description:
Papua New Guinea relies on paper-based patient records that often get lost, damaged, or remain unavailable during emergencies. This creates serious challenges for rural communities that travel long distances to access care.

This use case proposes to establish a unified national health information platform. It uses SevisPass Digital ID to verify patient identity and create secure health profiles. Registered individuals will have a digital health profile accessible across participating hospitals and clinics. Healthcare providers confirm identity via biometric authentication on the platform rather than via manual forms. Rural clinics can operate offline and sync data after connectivity returns.

The system will also include SMS reminders and a simple USSD service to ensure inclusive access. Patients receive notifications via SMS to visit the clinic or log in to a portal to view secure results. These channels allow individuals to query their status, view secure results, or book an appointment.

Title: National digital ID-based digital farmer ID for inclusive and resilient agriculture in West Africa
KeyTerms: Biometric authentication, land rights, financial inclusion, fraud prevention, supply chain traceability, accessibility
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor biometric authentication for subsidy access and financial transactions
Description:
West African farmers, who comprise 70% of the population, face widespread fraud and exclusion in accessing financial support from the government. Intermediaries divert about 40% of agricultural subsidies, while land conflicts account for 60% of rural disputes.

This use case idea proposes a platform that uses a biometric authentication service provided by the national digital identity system to address these challenges. Farmers must register on the platform using their national digital ID. Once registered, a farmer's digital ID is issued, and farmers can authenticate with fingerprints at mobile kiosks or use USSD with a PIN or OTP to link their bank account with the platform. This allows direct subsidy payments and removes intermediaries.

The farmer’s digital ID is also used to authenticate them and link their profile to their land title records. This platform also enables the sharing of farmers’ credit scores with financial organizations, based on past data.
The platform also supports harvest traceability for individual farmers, which enables access to microloans for unbanked farmers. Each harvest receives a digital “product passport” linked to the farmer ID, which enables market access via QR codes. Farmers can use USSD on basic phones without the Internet, as long as GSM coverage is available. For areas that lack network connectivity, agent devices support offline data capture and synchronization once connectivity is restored.

Title: Digital ID-enabled AI platform for farmer empowerment and financial access
KeyTerms: Digital innovation, AI-driven agriculture, financial inclusion, local language support, climate resilience, sustainable farming
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication for subsidy applications and financial transaction access
Description:
Small farmers in Africa face several challenges due to a lack of official documentation. These challenges prevent them from 
accessing formal credit, subsidy programs, access to markets and extension services.

This use case proposes a digital ID-based platform that uses AI to support farmers. Each farmer receives a unique farmer ID linked to their national digital ID. This farmer ID stores land and produce-related data, such as land size, crop type, and production history. The platform provides personalized advice on irrigation, soil health, planting cycles, and pest control. It supports local languages to improve access in rural areas.

It also simplifies access to subsidies and microcredit through AI-based eligibility checks for various institutional lenders.
The platform will also include training modules, disease-detection tools, weather alerts, and other features to improve farmers’ productivity.

Title: Issuance of a driving license using the National Digital ID
KeyTerms: Public services, digital identity, fraud reduction, process efficiency, citizen access
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - QR code-based single-factor authentication for license management and traffic verification systems
Description:
Many African countries still use manual, paper-based driver licensing systems that are vulnerable to fraud and data errors. Traffic officers cannot detect suspended driving licenses or fake permits because they lack reliable roadside verification tools.

The proposed use case will enable transport authorities to use a national digital ID authentication service to issue a driving license and provide roadside verification. When a citizen applies for a driving license, the system uses the national digital ID e-KYC service to verify their identity. On successful verification, the driving licenses will be issued, which will be linked to the respective citizens’ national digital ID. 

The digital license will be a cryptographically signed credential. Citizens can store it in a digital license app or carry it as a QR code card. Traffic police can scan the code with a dedicated app to verify these licenses instantly, even without an internet connection.

Title: eKYC for SIM card issuance and mobile money registrations using the national digital ID
KeyTerms: Mobile money, fraud prevention, biometric authentication, SIM registration, digital inclusion
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication
Description:
Many countries in Eastern Africa, such as Malawi, face a growing problem of mobile money fraud. The current agent-based registration process for SIM card issuance and FinTech accounts onboarding is done without strong identity verification. This gap allows fraudsters to create fake accounts.

This use case proposes a linkage of SIM cards and mobile money accounts to a person’s national digital ID using MOSIP’s identity authentication and e-KYC services. At SIM issuance, the telecom agent will authenticate the user by using biometrics, such as a fingerprint or facial image, along with the national digital ID credential. 

The platform will also require biometric checks for high-risk actions, such as SIM swaps or mobile money account registrations linked to the phone numbers. The user must also repeat biometric authentication within 24 hours to confirm these actions and avoid the creation of fake accounts. Any mismatch or repeated attempts trigger fraud alerts and block suspicious accounts.

Title: Digital ID-enabled warehouse system to reduce post-harvest loss in agriculture
KeyTerms: Renewable energy, rural development, financial inclusion, digital marketplace
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Face-based authentication in case of the government audit of the warehouse, or for product verification in case of digital market access
Description:
In recent years, post-harvest losses in Senegal’s agriculture sector have been estimated at 50–70%. These losses force farmers to sell produce at minimal prices to lenders, while consumers struggle to access quality produce at an affordable price

This use case proposes an application that will use a national digital ID-linked storage system to enable farmers to access refrigerated and dry warehouses. Farmers use a national digital ID to create a verified profile on the app. The app displays available storage space in nearby government-owned or government-registered warehouses. Based on estimated harvest volumes, farmers can pay a booking fee to reserve storage space in advance. 

Warehouses also offer access to an online marketplace for a service fee, which enables farmers to sell produce when prices are favorable. The use case ensures transparency by requiring all stored food grains to be linked digitally to the farmer’s ID. Warehouses that do not comply face penalties or deregistration.

Title: Digital ID-based agricultural marketplace for West African farmers
KeyTerms: Agriculture, digital marketplace, fraud prevention, financial inclusion, digital inclusion, AI chatbot, training and development, rural access
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - OTP-based authentication for marketplace access and agricultural transactions
Description:
Farmers in West Africa have limited access to markets and consequently lack real-time information on competitive prices for their crops. This use case proposes a digital agriculture marketplace platform. It features verified farmer profiles linked to their national digital IDs.

Farmers register on the platform with an OTP-based verification. They use the national digital ID to create their farmer profile. Verified farmers can list their produce for sale. This can include details, such as crop type, quantity, quality, location, and photos. Buyers from different regions also register as verified users on this platform, which builds trust on both sides of the transaction. On-ground agents authenticate uploaded information in response to requests from verified buyers.

The platform will also feature a resource hub that shares agricultural news, best farming practices, weather updates, and information on grants and support programs from trusted institutions. A mobile-first design and local language support ensure easy access for rural users.

Title: Integrating national digital ID for donor verification and blood inventory tracking
KeyTerms: Social Protection, Digital Identity, Mobile Device, Voice Interface, Accessibility, Emergency Response, Predictive Analytics
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - Single-factor PIN-based authentication for donor access and donation history
Description:
Blood banks across West and Central African countries often lack reliable digital records to identify repeat donors, track blood units, and quickly find compatible blood during emergencies.

This use case proposes the establishment of a national digital ID–enabled donor registry. The blood bank will register each donor using face authentication services provided by the national digital ID. Each verified individual national digital ID will be linked to the unique donor ID, which would serve as a portable digital health credential. The proposed donor registry stores these IDs, along with essential data such as blood group, donation history, and availability status.

Every blood unit has key details tagged as a QR code, which include the donor's ID, collection date, blood type, and expiration date. This ensures full traceability from donor to blood unit by all the stakeholders.

When hospitals raise emergency requests, blood banks use the registry to send digital alerts to eligible donors through a mobile or web application. The donor confirms his/her availability using digital ID authentication, enabling immediate matching.

Title: Digital ID-based land registration and solar energy allotment to farmers
KeyTerms: Agriculture, Energy Access, Land Rights, Blockchain, IoT Monitoring, Renewable Energy, Climate Resilience, Financial Inclusion
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multi-factor authentication for land registration and solar kit access (facial recognition and OTP)
Description:
Rural areas in Morocco lack reliable access to electricity. The government addressed this gap through renewable energy programs that install solar energy systems on farmland. However, these programs face challenges due to the absence of formal land titles in rural areas.

This use case proposes an application that links Morocco’s national digital ID (CNIE) to the land registration process in rural areas. This will help the government allocate solar installations fairly based on land ownership. Government agents map land boundaries using this application during field visits. The identity of the landholder is verified using CNIE-based facial recognition. Once verified, each parcel of land is assigned a unique digital land ID linked to the CNIE of the legal landholder.

Land parcels are also categorized as farmland, residential areas, or community land based on their use, which is recorded against the respective digital land ID. The energy department analyzes land ownership and installs solar systems on eligible properties based on size, use, and productivity. During installation, officials verify land ownership using CNIE-based verification services.

Title: Digital platform-led integration and inclusion in agriculture services through digital identity
KeyTerms: Digital inclusion and accessibility, biometric verification, blockchain, financial services, supply chain transparency, training and development
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 1 - OTP based authentication for financial services access and subsidy distribution
Description:
In many East African countries, farmers lack a single digital platform for farming advice, loans, insurance, and markets. Consequently, they lack accurate information on farm inputs. They also struggle to get credit and sell their produce. This use case proposes a digital farmer registry linked to the national digital ID. 

Trained agents enroll farmers using national digital ID credentials and biometric authentication during in-person visits. The registry links each national digital ID to its respective farmer profile. This profile comprises verified demographic data, land ownership records, crop types, farm size, and farming practices. It also links financial information, such as bank account details, income history, and credit indicators. These details create a complete agroeconomic profile. 

Farmers can share their profiles securely with approved public and private entities via OTP-based consent. For instance, banking institutions use this profile to assess farmer creditworthiness, and governments use it to distribute subsidies directly. The registry can be further developed to ease supply chain issues faced by farmers.

Title: Digital ID-enabled personal healthcare data sharing among healthcare organizations
KeyTerms: Digital health records, patient identity, emergency care, biometric authentication, medical data integration, public key infrastructure (PKI)
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Multifactor authentication by patients
Description:
Healthcare providers lack timely access to reliable medical records of patients. This issue causes delays in emergency care, misdiagnoses, and treatment errors. This use case proposes linking personal health records (PHRs) to an individual’s digital IDs.

These records would contain identification details, medical history, medications, allergies, blood type, immunization history, diagnostic data, and legal health documents, among others. Authorized healthcare institutions can access it through a PKI framework. This framework uses a dedicated national healthcare certificate authority (CA), regional healthcare CAs, or both. 

All data access requires patient consent via biometric authentication at the healthcare institution. This ensures secure access to sensitive records. The digital health records are shared through an encrypted channel. Healthcare providers access only data subsets based on their role and the patient’s consent. These transactions are subject to audit, which ensures accountability.

Title: Registration for unorganized works (E-Shram Portal)
KeyTerms: Informal sector, Worker welfare, Social protection, National database
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Aadhaar-based biometric verification
Description:
Digital ID is used to create a comprehensive National Database of Unorganized Workers (NDUW), verified and seeded with Aadhaar. This database enables delivery of targeted welfare programs for India’s vast informal workforce. 

The E-Shram portal was launched on 26th August 2021 by the Ministry of Labour and Employment. It registers unorganized workers, which include construction workers, migrant workers, gig and platform workers, street vendors, domestic workers, agricultural laborers, and others who lack formal employment contracts and social security coverage. During registration, workers provide their Aadhaar number for identity verification and e-KYC, along with occupation details, skill sets, and bank account information. The system generates a unique 12-digit Universal Account Number (UAN) for each registered worker and issues a digital E-Shram card. 

As of December 2024, the E-Shram portal has registered 304.8 million unorganized workers. This constitutes the world’s largest database of informal sector workers. The Aadhaar-verified database enables the government to identify beneficiaries and deliver welfare schemes directly to registered workers’ bank accounts using the JAM (Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile) trinity. As of the latest data, 12 central government programs have been integrated with E-Shram. These include the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY), which provides accidental insurance coverage, and the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), which provides life insurance. It also includes the Atal Pension Yojana (APY) for old-age pension, the National Pension Scheme (NPS), health insurance schemes, skill development programs, and maternity benefits.

Title: Registration of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (Udyam Portal)
KeyTerms: MSME registration, Business licensing, Entrepreneurship, eKYC
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Aadhaar-based e-KYC authentication
Description:
Digital ID is used to verify the identity of business owners or authorized signatories during MSME registration process. This enables a paperless and online registration process.

 The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises launched the Udyam Registration Portal on 1st July 2020 in collaboration with the UIDAI. It provides a unified, simplified registration system for MSMEs across India. The portal uses Aadhaar-based e-KYC to instantly verify the identity of entrepreneurs who apply for MSME registration. This eliminates the need for physical document submission and enables self-registration from anywhere. Business owners provide their Aadhaar number during registration, which validates their identity against the UIDAI database and auto-fills demographic details, such as their name and address. The platform also integrates with the Income Tax Department and GSTN (Goods and Services Tax Network) to auto-populate business financial data, which includes investment in plant and machinery and annual turnover based on PAN and GSTN, further simplifying the registration process. Upon successful registration, enterprises receive a permanent 16-digit Udyam Registration Number (URN) and a digital certificate. 

As of May 27, 2025, a total of 64.09 million MSMEs have registered on the Udyam portal. Udyam registration enables MSMEs to access various government schemes and benefits, which include the Credit Guarantee Scheme (CGTMSE) for collateral-free loans, Public Procurement Policy mandating 25% government procurement from MSMEs, subsidies and incentives for technology upgrades, priority sector lending status from banks, and protection under the Delayed Payment Act.

Title: Easy withdrawal and claims processing for employee provident funds
KeyTerms: Social security, Retirement savings, Provident fund, Claims processing
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Aadhaar-based authentication
Description:
Digital ID is linked to Universal Account Numbers (UANs) to facilitate seamless withdrawal and claims processing for employee provident fund benefits. The Ministry of Labour and Employment’s Employees’ Provident Fund Organization (EPFO) has collaborated with the UIDAI to integrate Aadhaar with the UAN system.

The UAN is a unique 12-digit number allotted to every EPFO member, which remains the same throughout their career, even when changing employers. It serves as a portable and permanent provident fund account identifier. Aadhaar-UAN linking enables employees to verify their identity during provident fund operations, which include EPF withdrawals, pension claims, transfer of funds between employers, and updating KYC details. Members can link their Aadhaar to their UAN through the EPFO Unified Member Portal or the UMANG app. They can provide their Aadhaar number and validate it through OTP authentication. As of September 2021, 94% of UANs have been seeded with Aadhaar, which represents millions of formal sector workers. The Aadhaar-UAN integration has enabled several innovations, which include paperless and presence-less claim settlement. Employees can submit EPF withdrawal claims online and do not need to visit EPFO offices or submit physical documents. Their claims are processed and approved within days, based on Aadhaar authentication. The system also supports the EPFO’s Automation of Field Offices (AFO) initiative and enables auto-settlement of claims under specified limits. The Aadhaar-EPFO integration has transformed social security administration in India as it enables instant, paperless provident fund claim settlement without employer attestation for Aadhaar-verified members. This reduces claim processing time from months to days or even hours, and eliminates the need for physical document submission and office visits. The integration also prevents fraudulent claims through biometric identity verification, facilitates portability of provident fund accounts across employers, supports financial security for more than 70 million formal sector workers, and ensures retirement savings reach rightful beneficiaries promptly.

Title: Use of Aadhaar in railway ticket booking
KeyTerms: Rail travel, e-Ticketing, Tatkal booking, Passenger verification
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Aadhaar OTP-based authentication
Description:
Digital ID is used to verify a passenger’s identity during railway ticket booking, particularly for Tatkal or last-minute reservations, and to add passengers to traveler master lists. Introduced in 2016, the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) implemented Aadhaar-based authentication for railway ticket bookings in collaboration with the UIDAI. This prevents ticket touting, reduces fraudulent bookings, and ensures genuine passengers receive reservations. Aadhaar OTP-based authentication became mandatory for Tatkal ticket bookings, a quota that allows last-minute reservations from one day before the journey date, and was highly susceptible to automated bulk bookings by touts. 

Passengers who book Tatkal tickets must provide their Aadhaar number and authenticate using a one-time password (OTP) sent to their Aadhaar-registered mobile number. This ensures only verified individuals can make such bookings. Additionally, passengers can add frequently traveled companions to their IRCTC master list by providing their Aadhaar numbers. This enables faster future bookings with pre-verified passenger details. During ticket checking on trains, traveling ticket examiners (TTEs) verify passenger identity by matching travel documents with government-issued IDs, which include Aadhaar. The Aadhaar integration addresses the chronic problem of ticket black marketing, where touts use automated software to bulk-book Tatkal tickets and resell them at inflated prices, which deprived genuine passengers. After implementation, the Indian Railways reported a significant reduction in touting activities.

Title: Highway Toll Payment - FASTag (KYC)
KeyTerms: Electronic toll collection, RFID, eKYC, Digital payments, Transport infrastructure
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Aadhaar-based e-KYC authentication
Description: Digital ID is used for electronic know your customer (e-KYC) verification during FASTag registration. It enabled instant issuance of electronic toll collection tags. FASTag was launched in 2016 by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) in collaboration with the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), the UIDAI, and authorized banks. It is a radio frequency identification (RFID) device affixed to vehicle windshields that enables automatic deduction of toll charges without the need for vehicles to stop at toll plazas. Vehicle owners must complete KYC verification to obtain a FASTag. Aadhaar-based e-KYC has become the preferred method due to its speed and convenience. Customers can register for a FASTag through multiple channels, which include bank branches, point-of-sale locations at toll plazas, online banking portals, and mobile apps. Customers have to provide their Aadhaar number for instant identity verification against the UIDAI database. The Aadhaar e-KYC process retrieves the applicant’s verified name, address, and photograph, which eliminates the need for physical document submission and enables instant FASTag activation. The system also requires vehicle registration details to link the FASTag to the specific vehicle. FASTag became mandatory for all class M & N vehicles in India from February 2021, driving rapid adoption. As of April 2025, more than 108.5 million FASTags have been issued. Aadhaar played a key role to enable seamless e-KYC during registration.

Title: CoWIN (COVID-19 Vaccination) - Use of Aadhaar in vaccination registration
KeyTerms: Vaccination management, Immunization, Certificate issuance, Public health
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Aadhaar-based verification or alternative ID verification
Description:
Digital ID is used as a primary identification method to book vaccination appointments and issue digital vaccination certificates. Launched in 2021 by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), the COVID-19 Vaccine Intelligence Network (CoWIN) is India’s digital platform that managed the world’s largest COVID-19 vaccination program. CoWIN enables citizens to register for vaccination, book appointments at nearby vaccination centers, and receive digital vaccination certificates. Beneficiaries can register with multiple forms of identification, such as Aadhaar, driving license, PAN card, passport, voter ID, pension passbook, NPR smart card, or other government-issued photo IDs.

Aadhaar served as the preferred and most widely used ID due to its universal coverage and instant verification capabilities. After the registration with Aadhaar or an alternative ID, beneficiaries receive SMS notifications for appointment confirmation and can walk into vaccination centers where their identity is verified against the registered details. Upon vaccination, the system instantly generates a digitally verifiable vaccination certificate that contains the beneficiary’s name, ID details, vaccine type, dose number, vaccination date, and a QR code for international verification. In total, more than 2.2 billion vaccination doses were administered through the CoWIN platform, which makes it one of the largest and fastest vaccination drives in human history. 

The CoWIN-Aadhaar integration enabled India to achieve a massive vaccination scale. It provided real-time tracking of vaccine inventory and distribution across 1 million+ vaccination sessions, which prevented duplicate vaccinations through unique ID verification, and enabled beneficiaries to receive dose reminders through SMS to Aadhaar-linked mobile numbers. It generated internationally recognized digital vaccination certificates crucial for travel, facilitated transparent monitoring of vaccination coverage across demographics and geographies, and supported India’s successful COVID-19 response that achieved more than 90% adult population coverage with at least one dose.

Title: Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) - Creation of health ID using Aadhaar
KeyTerms: Digital health, Health records, Unified Health Interface
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Aadhaar-based authentication (biometric or OTP)
Description:
Digital ID is voluntarily used to create a unique health identifier. The Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA), formerly known as Health ID, was launched in 2021 by the National Health Authority (NHA). This initiative was part of the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM).

ABHA is a 14-digit unique health identification number that serves as a digital gateway to an individual’s longitudinal health records. It enables seamless sharing of health information across hospitals, diagnostic centers, pharmacies, insurance companies, and telemedicine platforms. 

Citizens can voluntarily create their ABHA with Aadhaar-based authentication, through OTP or biometric. The ABHA system links to personal health records (PHRs) stored in digital lockers accessible through the ABHA mobile app or participating healthcare applications. This enables patients to share their medical history, prescriptions, diagnostic reports, discharge summaries, and immunization records with healthcare providers on a consent basis. As of December 2024, a total of 711.6 million Ayushman Bharat health accounts have been created.

Title: Linkage of tax ID (PAN) with Aadhaar
KeyTerms: Tax identification, Financial transactions, Tax compliance, Identity deduplication
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Aadhaar-based verification and deduplication
Description:
Digital ID is used to verify and uniquely link Permanent Account Number (PAN) to Aadhaar, which creates a unified tax identification system. Operational since 2017 and made mandatory in 2019 (with extensions), the Income Tax Department, in collaboration with the UIDAI, requires all PAN holders to link their PAN with their Aadhaar number. PAN is a 10-character alphanumeric identifier issued by the Income Tax Department to track financial transactions and tax compliance, while Aadhaar provides a biometric-based unique identity. The PAN-Aadhaar linkage serves to eliminate duplicate and fake PAN cards, ensure unique tax identification, and enable cross-verification of taxpayer information. 

Taxpayers can link their PAN with Aadhaar through multiple channels, which include the Income Tax e-filing portal, SMS to a designated number with their PAN and Aadhaar details, or PAN-Aadhaar linking facilities at banks and service centers. As of January 2024, more than 510 million PANs have been successfully linked with Aadhaar. The Income Tax Act was amended to make PAN-Aadhaar linking mandatory. Unlinked PANs became inoperative, which means they cannot be used for financial transactions, such as opening bank accounts, purchasing property, or filing income tax returns. The PAN-Aadhaar linkage system has strengthened India’s tax administration. It eliminated duplicate and bogus PAN cards estimated in millions, which enabled the detection of tax evasion through the identification of individuals who hold multiple PANs. The system supported the government’s efforts to expand the tax base and improve compliance, which facilitated seamless verification of taxpayer identity across financial and tax systems, reduced identity fraud in high-value financial transactions that require PAN, and created a strong, unique taxpayer identification infrastructure that integrates India’s tax and identity ecosystems.

Title: Voluntary use of Aadhaar for passport application
KeyTerms: Passport issuance, Travel document, Identity verification, Consular services
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Aadhaar-based identity validation
Description: Digital ID is voluntarily used to validate applicant identity during passport application processes before the Passport Verification or Granting Officer. Operational since 2015, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), in collaboration with the UIDAI, has accepted Aadhaar as a valid proof of identity and address during passport applications through the Passport Seva portal. Applicants can voluntarily mention their Aadhaar number in the online passport application form, which can then be used by passport seva kendras (PSKs) and passport offices to verify the applicant’s identity and address details against the UIDAI database during document verification. After the Supreme Court’s 2018 judgment on Aadhaar, the use of Aadhaar for passport applications is voluntary, and applicants can submit alternative identity and address proof documents if they choose not to use Aadhaar. However, Aadhaar can simplify the application process as it reduces the number of supporting documents required and accelerates verification. Applicants who provide Aadhaar do not need to submit additional proof of identity, such as a voter ID, a driving license, or a PAN card, and proof of address, such as utility bills or rental agreements, as Aadhaar serves dual purpose of identity and address verification. The Aadhaar integration supports streamlined passport application processing, which enables faster identity and address verification by passport officers, reduces manual scrutiny of multiple physical documents, and prevents duplicate passport applications through Aadhaar uniqueness.

Title: Property registration and land records
KeyTerms: Land administration, Property rights, eKYC, Stamp duty, Real estate
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Aadhaar-based biometric and e-KYC authentication
Description:
Digital ID is used for identity verification of buyers and sellers during property registration and land transactions. Since 2015, various state governments across India, has integrated Aadhaar-based e-KYC into property registration systems to verify the identities of parties involved in property transactions. 
During property registration at sub-registrar offices, buyers, sellers, and witnesses must authenticate their identities using Aadhaar-based biometric verification, which can be a fingerprint or iris scan, or e-KYC. This retrieves verified demographic details directly from the UIDAI database. This system has been implemented in multiple states, which include Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Uttar Pradesh, as part of their Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP). 

Aadhaar authentication ensures that only the genuine property owner can execute sale deeds or transfer documents, which prevents impersonation and fraudulent transactions. The integration also facilitates linkage with the Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP) and digitization of land records under initiatives, such as the Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas (SVAMITVA).

Title: Filing income-tax returns using Aadhaar
KeyTerms: Tax compliance, e-Filing, Digital verification, Revenue administration
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Aadhaar OTP authentication
Description:
Digital ID is used for electronic verification of income tax returns, which enables instant validation without the need for physical document submission. The Income Tax Department, in collaboration with the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), allows taxpayers to e-verify their filed income tax returns (ITRs) through Aadhaar-based one-time password (OTP) authentication. 

Taxpayers must verify their return within 30 days of filing an ITR through the Income Tax e-filing portal for it to be considered valid. Aadhaar-based e-verification has become the most popular verification method, which allows taxpayers to instantly verify their returns by receiving an OTP on their Aadhaar-registered mobile number and entering it on the e-filing portal. 

For the assessment year 2024-25 (till 31st July 2024), more than 62.1 million ITRs were e-verified, of which more than 58.1 million used Aadhaar-based OTP, which represents 93.6% of all e-verified returns. This method has largely replaced older verification processes. These methods include submission of a physically signed income tax return verification form (ITR-V) by post to the Centralized Processing Center (CPC) in Bengaluru, net banking verification, bank ATM verification, and Demat account verification. 

The Aadhaar-based e-verification system has enhanced tax compliance in India by providing instant return verification without requiring taxpayers to print, sign, and mail physical documents. It reduces the ITR processing time from weeks to days, eliminating verification delays that previously led to delayed refunds. 

The system ensures secure authentication through government-verified biometric identity, which lowers compliance costs for taxpayers and administrative costs for the Income Tax Department. This system also supports India’s digital tax administration transformation under the Digital India initiative.

Title: Jeevan Pramaan (Digital Life Certificate)
KeyTerms: Pension verification, Biometric authentication, Life certificate, Pensioner services
AuthenticationAssuranceLevel: AAL 2 - Fingerprint or iris biometric authentication
Description:
Digital ID is used for biometric authentication to generate digital life certificates for pensioners, which eliminates the need for physical verification. The Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, in collaboration with the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) and banks, launched Jeevan Pramaan in November 2014. 

Pensioners submit a life certificate annually, typically in November, to confirm they are alive and eligible to continue receiving pension payments. The Jeevan Pramaan system enables pensioners to submit their annual life certificate digitally through Aadhaar-based biometric authentication, which removes the need to appear physically before pension disbursing authorities. 
 
Jeevan Pramaan allows pensioners to authenticate their identity through fingerprint or iris scan at designated service centers, Common Service Centers (CSCs), or through the Jeevan Pramaan mobile app. This app requires phone-based camera to complete Aadhaar-based face authentication. The system instantly generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is directly transmitted to the Pension Disbursing Agency, such as a bank or government department. This eliminates paperwork and manual submission. 

During 1st–11th November 2024, 4.81 million DLC were generated, which demonstrates widespread adoption of this digital service among India’s elderly population. The Jeevan Pramaan system has transformed pension administration by providing convenience to senior citizens who previously had to travel to pension offices. It reduces administrative burden on pension disbursing agencies, prevents delays in pension payments due to late certificate submission, and enables pensioners living abroad to submit certificates through designated centers.
